jobs.title: Senior Director of Software Engineering (Infrastructure)
jobs.description:
Job Description

Your opportunity to make a real impact and shape the future of financial services is waiting for you. Let's push the boundaries of what's possible together.

As a Senior Director of Software Engineering at JPMorganChase within the Card Technology organization, you lead multiple technical areas, manage the activities of multiple departments, and collaborate across technical domains. Your expertise is applied cross-functionally to drive the adoption and implementation of technical methods within various teams and aid the firm in remaining at the forefront of industry trends, best practices, and technological advances.

Job Responsibilities

Lead multiple technology and process implementations across departments to achieve firmwide technology objectives.
Directly manage multiple areas with strategic transactional focus, balancing speed, risk, resiliency, and cost-to-serve outcomes.
Set and scale multi-department strategy for agentic AI-enabled engineering and SDLC/TLM automation (using enterprise-authorized tools within the work environment) to drive firmwide objectives (speed, scalability, reliability, and cost-to-serve), including portfolio-level standards for AI-orchestrated delivery workflows, release governance, automated test modernization, resilience engineering, and incident response acceleration; establish guardrails for validation, security, resiliency, traceability, and reuse.
Drive cloud-native platform modernization across teams, including Kubernetes-based application/platform enablement, standardized deployment patterns, and production readiness practices.
Lead infrastructure-as-code adoption and portfolio standards using Terraform, enabling repeatable, compliant provisioning across environments.
Define and enforce multi-region cloud architecture patterns (active/active and active/passive where appropriate) to improve availability, resiliency, and recovery objectives.
Apply deep knowledge of the SDLC toolchain including enterprise-authorized AI-assisted development, CI/CD automation, and release controls to increase engineering throughput and reliability.
Partner with security and controls to strengthen cloud identity and access practices, including AWS IAM design, least-privilege access, and traceable approvals for sensitive actions.
Establish resilience engineering programs including failure-mode testing and game days; accelerate incident response through automation and standardized runbooks (including chaos engineering tooling such as Gremlin where authorized).
Provide leadership and high-level direction to teams while overseeing employee populations across multiple platforms, divisions, and lines of business.
Act as the primary interface with senior leaders, stakeholders, and executives, driving consensus across competing objectives and large cross-product collaborations.

Required Qualifications, Capabilities, And Skills

Formal training or certification on software engineering concepts and 10+ years applied experience; 5+ years leading technologists to solve complex technical problems within your domain.
Experience developing and/or leading large and cross-functional teams of technologists, including hiring, developing, and recognizing talent.
Demonstrated ability to influence across highly matrixed organizations and deliver value at scale through standards, platforms, and operating model change.
Experience leading multi-organization adoption of agentic AI-enabled engineering operating models (using enterprise-authorized tools within the work environment), including governance (human-in-the-loop decisioning, quality gates), measurement frameworks, and secure handling of sensitive inputs/outputs across teams.
Deep understanding of responsible AI risk, controls, and resiliency/security expectations at scale, with the ability to advise senior leaders on safe adoption, portfolio governance, and reuse-first strategies.
Extensive practical cloud-native experience, including building and operating services on AWS.
Strong experience with Kubernetes (designing scalable workloads, platform enablement, operational patterns, and reliability practices in production).
Strong experience with infrastructure-as-code, especially Terraform, including modularization, policy/guardrails, and environment standardization.
Experience designing and operating multi-region cloud architectures, including HA/DR patterns, observability, and reliability targets (RTO/RPO).
Experience implementing secure identity and access controls in the cloud, including IAM concepts (least privilege, role-based access, and auditability).
Experience modernizing delivery pipelines and operational excellence practices, including CI/CD, automated testing, and resilience/chaos engineering approaches (e.g., Gremlin).

About Us

Chase is a leading financial services firm, helping nearly half of America's households and small businesses achieve their financial goals through a broad range of financial products. Our mission is to create engaged, lifelong relationships and put our customers at the heart of everything we do. We also help small businesses, nonprofits and cities grow, delivering solutions to solve all their financial needs.

We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash and/or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.

We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

Equal Opportunity Employer/Disability/Veterans

About The Team

Our Consumer & Community Banking division serves our Chase customers through a range of financial services, including personal banking, credit cards, mortgages, auto financing, investment advice, small business loans and payment processing. We're proud to lead the U.S. in credit card sales and deposit growth and have the most-used digital solutions – all while ranking first in customer satisfaction.

jobs.description:
As Marqeta's Senior Manager, Software Engineering,
you will lead and evolve our Credit onboarding team. This is a critical leadership role responsible for scaling the next generation of innovative credit onboarding platforms that power modern fintech experiences.

You will lead the Credit onboarding engineering team responsible for building, operating, and modernizing core components of our credit platform. This role requires a leader who sets a high bar, moves with urgency, and brings clarity in complex environments.

You will partner closely with Product, Data, Risk, Compliance, and Operations to define strategy, drive execution, and deliver resilient, secure, and highly available systems at scale. We work Flexible First. This role can be performed remotely anywhere in the United States.

This position is for an existing vacancy.

The Impact You’ll Have

Own the end-to-end Credit onboarding platform responsible for new credit customers onboarding.
Drive platform resiliency, scalability, and operational excellence
Drive AI-first automation, reducing manual handling and increasing efficiency across dispute classification, evidence management, and prioritization.
Partner with Product to shape roadmap, sequencing, and delivery strategy
Lead and mentor a high-performing team, improving engineering velocity and system reliability through intelligent workflows and automation.
Establish clear engineering standards around quality, reliability, testing, and documentation
Improve execution rigor including planning, sprint hygiene, and measurable outcomes
Lead architectural discussions and make high quality technical decisions
Stay close to the codebase and system design while empowering teams to execute
Recruit and develop top engineering talent and actively build bench strength
Create a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement

Who You Are

Experienced engineering leader (8–12+ years in engineering, 4+ years managing senior engineers or managers).
Experience building and scaling distributed systems in cloud native environments, preferably AWS
Strong background in microservices architectures and high availability systems
Proven ability to operate in regulated or compliance sensitive environments
Experience in fintech strongly preferred; credit domain experience is a plus but not required
Demonstrated track record of raising engineering standards and improving execution discipline
Comfortable navigating ambiguity while driving clarity and momentum
High personal standards and a bias toward action

What Will Set You Apart

Experience building or scaling credit products such as underwriting, ledgering, servicing, or transaction processing
Experience improving platform resiliency such as multi region architectures
Track record of evolving teams from good to great
Masters Degree in Computer Science

Your Manager

Pramod Rao

Marqeta is powering the most well known brands in the new economy (Block, Cash App, Affirm, Instacart, Doordash, Uber, Walmart, etc). jobs.title: Director, Commercial Process & Technology - Surgical
jobs.description:
We anticipate the application window for this opening will close on - 24 Aug 2026

Careers that change lives start here. Medtronic is a global leader in healthcare technology with a Mission to alleviate pain, restore health, and extend life. Our 95,000 employees work across more than 150 countries to put patients first — developing innovative medical technologies that improve the lives of 72+ million patients each year. Your unique talents will help shape the future of healthcare while building a career grounded in purpose, growth, and impact.

A Day in the Life

At Medtronic, we bring bold ideas forward with speed and decisiveness to put patients first in everything we do. This position is remote to enhance our competitive edge and expand our cross-functional collaboration efforts. This role will require 20% of travel to enhance collaboration and ensure successful completion of projects.

The Director, Commercial Process & Digital Transformation will support the US Surgical business and is responsible for defining, optimizing, and enabling commercial processes through technology. This leader serves as the Business Product Owner for core commercial platforms, including Salesforce.com and AI-enabled capabilities, while partnering closely with Sales, Marketing, IT, Data & Analytics, Finance and C&P functions to identify opportunities for simplification, automation, and digital transformation.

The role is accountable for defining future-state commercial processes, translating business needs into scalable technology solutions, establishing governance frameworks, managing business priorities, and ensuring successful adoption across the commercial organization. Success in this role requires balancing strategic vision with operational execution, ensuring technology investments drive measurable improvements in productivity, customer experience, commercial effectiveness, and business performance.

Key Responsibilities

Commercial Process Digitalization

Challenge existing processes and drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on effectiveness and efficiency.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, automate, and modernize workflows.
Define future-state operating models that leverage automation, digital tools, and AI capabilities.
Ensure business processes are scalable, sustainable, and aligned across Surgical businesses, regions and functions where appropriate

Business Product Ownership

Serve as Business Product Owner for Salesforce.com and designated AI-enabled platforms
Define the vision, roadmap, priorities, and success measures and ensure solutions are aligned to commercial strategy.
Manage and prioritize business requirements, enhancement requests, and use cases.
Establish intake and evaluation processes to ensure business needs are appropriately captured and prioritized.
Act as primary liaison between commercial stakeholders and technology delivery teams.

Commercial Technology Strategy

Develop and maintain a commercial technology roadmap aligned with organizational priorities and related functions (i.e C&P technology roadmap)
Drive integration and alignment across CRM, analytics, automation, AI, and related commercial technologies.
Partner with technology teams to ensure solutions meet business requirements.
Monitor industry trends and emerging technologies to identify innovation opportunities.

Governance & Portfolio Management

Establish governance processes for commercial technology investments and enhancement requests.
Create intake, prioritization, and decision-making frameworks to ensure transparency and alignment.
Lead prioritization of initiatives across competing business demands.
Ensure alignment between regional, global, and enterprise priorities.
Facilitate alignment across stakeholders and resolve competing business priorities.
Develop and maintain transparent reporting on project status, roadmap, risks, and value realization

Change Management and Adoption

Drive adoption of new technologies and business processes.
Develop communication, training, and stakeholder engagement strategies.
Define and track adoption, utilization, and business outcome metrics.
Promote a culture of continuous improvement and digital innovation.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree with at least 10+ years, or advanced degree with at least 8+ years of experience in Commercial Digital Transformation, SFDC Product Management, or related functions
7+ years of people, program or project management experience
Experience leading Salesforce.com (or other CRM) platform strategy and governance.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience serving as a Salesforce.com Business Product Owner and leading commercial technology initiatives (AI, automation, digital transformation initiatives)
Experience leading cross-functional projects in complex matrix organizations.
Demonstrated success driving business process transformation through technology solutions
Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and influencing skills.
Strong understanding of commercial processes, forecasting, pipeline management, and customer engagement workflows
Lean certification
Salesforce administrator certification or higher
Medical device, healthcare, life sciences, or other highly regulated industry experience.
Agile product management experience.
MBA or advanced degree.
Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, information systems, or related discipline.

For Baccalaureate degrees earned outside of the United States, a degree that satisfies the requirements of 8 C.F.R.

214.2(h)(4)(iii)(A) is required.

Physical Job Requirements

The above statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this position, but they are not an exhaustive list of all the required responsibilities and skills of this position. 

The physical demands described within the Responsibilities section of this job description are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. For Office Roles: While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to be independently mobile. The employee is also required to interact with a computer, and communicate with peers and co-workers. Contact your manager or local HR to understand the Work Conditions and Physical requirements that may be specific to each role.

U.S. Work Authorization & Sponsorship

At Medtronic, we are committed to fostering an environment where employees can thrive and make a meaningful impact. In alignment with our enterprise-wide workforce planning approach, U.S. work authorization sponsorship (H-1B, TN, J, etc.) is offered exclusively for Principal-level roles and above, where specialized expertise aligns with long-term business needs. Roles below the Principal level require candidates to possess unrestricted U.S. work authorization at the time of hire and for the duration of employment.

‌

Recruitment Fraud Alert

We are aware of phishing scams targeting job seekers. Please keep the following in mind:

Apply only through official Medtronic channels. All legitimate Medtronic recruiting communications come from approved Medtronic platforms and official @medtronic.com email addresses.

Medtronic will never ask for payment or sensitive personal information (such as bank account or Social Security details) during early stages of the hiring process. Any such requests are not legitimate.

If you receive a suspicious message claiming to be from Medtronic, do not respond, click links, or open attachments.

If you have any questions, concerns regarding the authenticity of a communication alleged to have been made by or on behalf of Medtronic, please contact us immediately at AskHR@medtronic.com.

jobs.description:
Thank you for considering Progyny!

Progyny is seeking a Director of IT who balances visionary leadership with deep-rooted technical expertise. This role is designed for a hands-on leader who has spent the last decade leading high-performing teams while remaining a subject matter expert in the core technology systems we use to deliver our technology experience to all users.

The ideal candidate will be the primary architect and guardian of our digital infrastructure, ensuring that our security posture, automation workflows, and identity management systems are best of breed. This role won’t just manage the department; it will set the technical standard for how we leverage our technology tools to leverage business performance.

We work in a team environment and expect a proactive approach to tackling our day-to-day tasks as well as jumping into priority and emergency situations.

What You'll Do...

Strategic Leadership: Direct the IT department's roadmap, aligning technology investments with organizational growth while managing a team of technical specialists.
Infrastructure & Security: Serve as the internal expert for Microsoft Entra (Identity) and Microsoft Defender, overseeing threat protection, conditional access policies, and enterprise-grade security protocols.
Endpoint Management: Architect and manage our global device footprint using Microsoft Intune & JAMF, ensuring seamless deployment, compliance, and patch management.
Business Automation: Lead the adoption of the Power Platform, specifically using Power Apps and Power Automate to digitize manual workflows and enhance departmental efficiency.
M365 Governance: Oversee the full Microsoft 365 tenant, ensuring optimal configuration of Teams, SharePoint, and Exchange while maintaining strict data governance.
AI in the workforce: Support the rollout and enablement of AI in the workforce and demonstrate the ability to use AI to strengthen the performance of the IT team and the business generally.

About You...

Bachelors or Masters in technical field or related experience.
10 years in IT leadership roles, with a proven track record of mentoring technical staff and managing vendor relationships.
Extensive hands-on experience as an individual contributor within the Microsoft ecosystem (Entra, Intune, Defender, and M365).
Deep proficiency in automation tools like Power Automate or n8n development and a history of building custom business solutions.
The ability to manage and build in the Microsoft Azure cloud solution and integrate with our business processes
Experience with compliance standards like SOC2, SOX, or other common control standards applied to technology systems.
The ability to translate complex technical vulnerabilities or architectural needs into clear business cases for executive leadership.
Team management experience with the ability to bring the best out of everyone on the team

Please note:
This is not a digital nomad or remote international position; candidates must be based in the United States. Progyny is unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Candidates must be authorized to work in United States without the need for sponsorship, now or in the future.

jobs.description:
As a Capital One Senior Director of Software Engineering, you'll work on everything from customer-facing web and mobile applications using cutting-edge open source frameworks, to highly-available RESTful microservices, to back-end Java based systems using the hottest techniques in Big Data. You'll bring solid experience in emerging and traditional technologies such as: node.js, Java, GO, AngularJS, React, Python, REST, JSON, XML, Ruby, Perl, NoSQL databases, relational databases, Hadoop, Chef, Maven, iOS, Android, and AWS/Cloud Infrastructure to name a few.

Our team builds the enterprise's premier engineering intelligence platform, empowering our entire technology organization to be fundamentally data-driven. Acting as an active insights engine for everyone from front-line developers to executive leadership, this platform delivers standardized, actionable metrics across the SDLC. By surfacing critical insights into engineering efficiency, development workflows, and modern tooling adoption, we equip teams with the exact analytics needed to pinpoint structural bottlenecks, eliminate developer friction, and accelerate time-to-market.

In this position, you will lead "Developer Experience for AI" here at Capital One. You will be evolving how Capital One developers engage with AI by delivering new AI tools, maturing the AI ecosystem, developing Capital One's AI Context Strategy, and more.

You will:

Lead, manage and grow multiple teams of product focused software engineers
Mentor and guide the professional and technical development of engineers on your team.
Work with product managers to understand desired application capabilities and testing scenarios
Continuously improve software engineering practices
Work within and across Agile teams to design, develop, test, implement, and support technical solutions across a full-stack development tools and technologies
Lead the craftsmanship, availability, resilience, and scalability of your solutions
Bring a passion to stay on top of tech trends, experiment with and learn new technologies, participate in internal & external technology communities, and mentor other members of the engineering community
Encourage innovation, implementation of cutting-edge technologies, inclusion, outside-of-the-box thinking, teamwork, self-organization, and diversity
Work across to improve the velocity of your and other teams
Lead efforts to deploy new and existing applications into AWS environments
Break existing monolithic applications into micro service architectures and build new microservices

Bachelor’s Degree
At least 9 years of experience in software engineering
At least 7 years of experience in people management

Master’s Degree in Computer Science or a Master’s Degree in Software Engineering

We are looking for a Director of Technology to lead our technology team and shape how technology powers the way we design, sell, and deliver world-class bike and hiking trips. This is a full-time, exempt position based at our Madison, Wisconsin office, with a hybrid schedule and regular in-office presence expected. This position reports directly to the President of Trek Travel.

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE, BUT NOT LIMITED TO:

Leadership & Team Development

Lead, mentor, and develop the technology team, including hiring, goal setting, performance management, and career development across IT, ecommerce, and development staff.
Provide support, training, and guidance to internal and external technology users, assessing computing needs and system requirements.

Strategy & Roadmap

Translate company vision into an enterprise systems strategy and multi-year technology roadmap, partnering with department heads and senior leadership to align technology with operational and strategic goals.
Lead planning and execution of company-wide technology initiatives, including project management, change management, and staff training across departments.

Systems, Infrastructure & AI

Own the architecture and integrations connecting our booking, ecommerce, ERP, CRM, and financial systems, including performance, reliability, and upgrades of core business systems and the Microsoft Power Platform environment.
Lead the ecommerce and software development functions, setting technical direction and quality standards for the team.
Develop and execute Trek Travel's AI strategy and governance standards, identifying high-impact opportunities to improve workflows and productivity while safeguarding data privacy and security.
Own the company's reporting data model, serving as steward of a single source of truth for business metrics.

Security & Compliance

Own the information security program, including risk management, endpoint protection, access controls, MFA, patching, and least-privilege reviews
Ensure cybersecurity and regulatory compliance across guest booking and payment systems (PCI-DSS, GDPR, state privacy laws), including annual assessments, penetration testing, and remediation.

Budget & Vendor Management

Oversee the technology department budget and manage vendor, consultant, and SaaS relationships across the full lifecycle — from selection and negotiation to renewal and performance review.

WHAT ELSE WE'D LIKE TO SEE FROM YOU:

Bachelor's degree and 8+ years of progressive technology experience, including 3+ years leading and developing technical teams.
Deep technical experience across IT management, programming, ERP systems, database administration and security, and web/application development.
A practical, hands-on technologist with strong technical architecture instincts and a well-rounded background across development, data, security, infrastructure, ecommerce, CRM, and ERP.
Excellent communication and analytical skills, with a solution-oriented, “how can I help” attitude and strong troubleshooting instincts.
Values hospitality and customer service, with an interest in the active travel industry a plus.

TREK TRAVEL OFFERS:

A fast-paced, casual, motivating, and fun company culture where initiative and pro-activity are highly valued.
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
Short- and long-term disability and life insurance
Paid parental leave
401(k) with company match
Generous PTO, paid holidays, and volunteer time off
Rewards for sustainable commuting
Employee and outdoor industry discounts

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager for Self-Serve (Learning)
jobs.description:
RDQ426R220

At Databricks, we are passionate about enabling data teams to solve the world's toughest problems — from making the next mode of transportation a reality to accelerating the development of medical breakthroughs. We do this by building and running the world's best data and AI infrastructure platform so our customers can use deep data insights to improve their business.

The Self-Serve team owns Databricks' product-led growth motion — the experience that takes someone from "I just heard about Databricks" to succeeding on the platform entirely on their own. Our most ambitious bet is Learning: making Databricks the place where anyone interested in data + AI comes to learn, and building the largest community of active, capable learners in the world. It's a long game with a simple thesis — if people learn data + AI on Databricks, it becomes ubiquitous with the field itself, driving adoption and revenue.

As a Senior Engineering Manager on the Self-Serve team, you will lead the Learning bet end to end across two sides: self-paced learning — a place to learn any Databricks skill, hands-on labs that spin up inside a real workspace, and a durable skill profile a learner carries across jobs — and enterprise-managed learning, giving admins the tools to assign, track, and grow learning inside their orgs. AI is central to both: a content-generation agent that scales the catalog far past what we could author by hand, and an AI tutor that guides learners hands-on inside the product. This is a genuine 0→1 product with real systems depth — on-demand provisioning, identity, sandboxing, and an interactive learning engine that must scale to millions of learners — and you'll grow and lead a team of ~12 engineers (planned to roughly double) to build it.

The Impact You Will Have

Strategy & Vision: Define and drive the technical and product strategy for Learning, and tie it into the broader self-serve growth motion.
Execution Ownership: Own the roadmap, execution, and delivery — taking a 0→1 product from early signal to millions of learners at the highest standards of quality.
Engineering Excellence: Establish team best practices — design reviews, code quality, testing, and performance for high-scale, interactive systems.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner closely across R&D, the Learning & Enablement org, Marketing (university and online channels), and Field Engineering to align the product with how learners actually reach and adopt Databricks.

What We Look For

Experience:
15+ years of software engineering experience with a strong track record of technical leadership and impact.
5+ years of engineering management experience, including 2+ years managing other managers (or clear readiness to).

jobs.description:
As a Capital One Senior Director of Software Engineering, you'll work on everything from customer-facing web and mobile applications using cutting-edge open source frameworks, to highly-available RESTful microservices, to back-end Java based systems using the hottest techniques in Big Data. You'll bring solid experience in emerging and traditional technologies such as: node.js, Java, GO, AngularJS, React, Python, REST, JSON, XML, Ruby, Perl, NoSQL databases, relational databases, Hadoop, Chef, Maven, iOS, Android, and AWS/Cloud Infrastructure to name a few.

Our team builds the enterprise's premier engineering intelligence platform, empowering our entire technology organization to be fundamentally data-driven. Acting as an active insights engine for everyone from front-line developers to executive leadership, this platform delivers standardized, actionable metrics across the SDLC. By surfacing critical insights into engineering efficiency, development workflows, and modern tooling adoption, we equip teams with the exact analytics needed to pinpoint structural bottlenecks, eliminate developer friction, and accelerate time-to-market.

In this position, you will lead "Developer Experience for AI" here at Capital One. You will be evolving how Capital One developers engage with AI by delivering new AI tools, maturing the AI ecosystem, developing Capital One's AI Context Strategy, and more.

You will:

Lead, manage and grow multiple teams of product focused software engineers
Mentor and guide the professional and technical development of engineers on your team.
Work with product managers to understand desired application capabilities and testing scenarios
Continuously improve software engineering practices
Work within and across Agile teams to design, develop, test, implement, and support technical solutions across a full-stack development tools and technologies
Lead the craftsmanship, availability, resilience, and scalability of your solutions
Bring a passion to stay on top of tech trends, experiment with and learn new technologies, participate in internal & external technology communities, and mentor other members of the engineering community
Encourage innovation, implementation of cutting-edge technologies, inclusion, outside-of-the-box thinking, teamwork, self-organization, and diversity
Work across to improve the velocity of your and other teams
Lead efforts to deploy new and existing applications into AWS environments
Break existing monolithic applications into micro service architectures and build new microservices

At least 7 years of experience in people management

jobs.description:
About Ode With Anthropic

How do you turn a decades-old dataset into an industry-leading medical coding agent? Teach an AI receptionist to book appointments in Spanish? Automatically generate working data connectors from API docs? Build agents that write, test, and deploy their own software packages?

Anthropic is defining frontier AI. Ode is the team bringing frontier AI into practice.

We are a team of experienced builders who care deeply about getting complex AI systems into production, with strong conviction about what makes them succeed. As Anthropic’s services venture, we tackle the hardest, most consequential AI problems for companies with real stakes, working closely with their Applied AI and Product teams to turn frontier technology into real world impact.

We're backed by Anthropic, Blackstone, Hellman & Friedman, Goldman Sachs, General Atlantic, Leonard Green & Partners, Apollo Global Management, GIC, and Sequoia Capital.

We're headquartered in SF with offices in NYC, Raleigh-Durham, and Dubai.

The Role

We're hiring a seasoned Operator to lead and grow our lean Business Operations and Analytics team from first principles.

The core mandate: build the systems, infrastructure and enabling process to stay one step ahead of scale while taking on the special projects to support step-wise changes in our growth.

Fractional AI is a true operations business: creating value by optimizing supply and demand. You’d own this critical intersection that’s the core of our business while writing the playbook for scaling in an AI native way.

What You'll Do

Build the infrastructure to scale: Build the systems, data, and processes that keep us ahead of growth. Approach internal operations like a product, using AI and automation to create better ways of working as we scale.
Lead critical strategic initiatives: Take on the cross-functional problems and opportunities that matter most to our next stage of growth—from new market expansion to new bets across the business.
Optimize supply and demand: Connect our commercial pipeline to our workforce through forecasting, capacity planning, and staffing—ensuring we have the right talent deployed against the right work while optimizing utilization and economics.
Drive company planning and performance: Own the rhythms that help us run the company—from annual and quarterly planning to internal communications, business reviews, and Board preparation.

What You Bring

You've scaled a high-growth business: You've helped build the systems and infrastructure behind a company through a period of rapid growth.
You bring exceptional analytical and technical rigor: You're highly quantitative, understand how data and systems work under the hood, and can build rigorous models from messy inputs.
You're a player-coach: You can build and lead an exceptional team while staying deeply in the work.
You build lean by design: You default to better systems, automation, and AI before adding people or process.
You want to win: You have a high bar, move with urgency, and are deeply motivated to build something exceptional.

Our Values

Overdeliver: We are writing the playbook on how to create enterprise value with LLMs, and building our reputation as the world’s best applied AI team.
Overuse AI: We obsessively explore and experiment with Claude to push the frontier of applied AI and share what we learn with our teammates.
Over “engineer” the Culture: We’re building a culture that attracts and retains top applied AI talent, and we stress test large decisions through the perspective of our world class builders.

jobs.title: Director, Systems Engineering
jobs.description:
Job Description

Position Summary

Cloud/Systems is a key domain within Southland's Infrastructure organization, focused on enabling secure, scalable, and reliable cloud-first technology services across the enterprise. This role supports the company's growth by driving consistency in how cloud platforms, identity services, M365 foundational services, and core enterprise systems are designed, governed, and operated.

As the Director, Systems Engineering, you will lead the strategy, standardization, and ongoing improvement of Southland's cloud infrastructure and systems platforms. This includes Microsoft Azure, M365 foundational services, Entra ID, core identity capabilities, infrastructure automation, platform governance, and the operational practices required to keep enterprise systems reliable and secure.

The focus is simple: make it easier for teams to scale securely, integrate new business needs quickly, operate cloud services consistently, and reduce risk through strong architecture, automation, governance, and operational discipline.

You will work closely with Cybersecurity, Network, Platform Engineering, Support Services, business leaders, and key vendors to ensure cloud and systems platforms support how the company operates today and how it needs to grow. Travel to offices or project locations will be required depending on business needs.

Position Details

Cloud Architecture & Platform Strategy

Lead the development and governance of enterprise cloud architecture with primary focus on Microsoft Azure, M365 foundational services, and cloud-first infrastructure capabilities.
Define and enforce standards for cloud compute, storage, platform services, tenant configuration, cloud-side networking dependencies, and core enterprise systems.
Establish repeatable architecture patterns, landing zones, naming standards, tagging standards, service models, and reference architectures that support growth and consistency.
Drive modernization through infrastructure-as-code, automation, standardized service deployment, and simplification of legacy or inconsistent system practices.
Ensure cloud architecture balances scalability, security, cost efficiency, resilience, and operational supportability.
Provide technical direction for cloud platform decisions, ensuring designs align with enterprise architecture, cybersecurity standards, and business priorities.
Translate business growth plans into practical cloud and systems roadmap decisions that can scale across divisions, offices, and project environments.

Identity & Access Management

Own the enterprise identity strategy as a core control plane for access, security, and platform integration.
Lead governance of Entra ID, authentication methods, role-based access control, conditional access, identity lifecycle management, and enterprise access patterns.
Partner with Cybersecurity to align privileged access, zero trust enforcement, identity protection, and access monitoring with enterprise security requirements.
Ensure identity services are designed to scale with organizational growth, acquisitions, new offices, new applications, and changing compliance requirements.
Establish standards for administrative access, service accounts, groups, application integrations, and identity-related operational processes.
Drive consistent identity practices across M365, Azure, SaaS integrations, infrastructure platforms, and business-facing services.

Cloud Operations & Reliability

Own the operational performance, reliability, and availability of cloud and systems platforms under the Cloud/Systems function.
Establish monitoring, alerting, logging, and observability practices that allow teams to detect issues early and reduce business impact.
Lead operational maturity efforts including incident response coordination, problem management, root cause analysis, change management, and continuous improvement.
Define and enforce configuration management, lifecycle management, backup, recovery, patching, and service health practices for cloud and systems platforms.
Ensure operational practices are scalable and repeatable rather than dependent on tribal knowledge or one-off manual processes.
Partner with Support and Platform Engineering to ensure clean handoffs, escalation paths, and visibility into platform issues that impact users.

Automation & Infrastructure Engineering

Drive automation of infrastructure provisioning, platform configuration, reporting, and recurring operational tasks.
Establish infrastructure-as-code standards using appropriate tools such as Terraform, Bicep, PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, or similar automation frameworks.
Promote reusable templates, modules, scripts, and deployment patterns that improve consistency and reduce manual effort.
Align infrastructure automation with change management, auditability, access control, and operational governance requirements.
Support the development of automated workflows for provisioning, deprovisioning, system configuration, and compliance reporting.
Create an engineering culture that favors repeatable, documented, and measurable solutions over ad hoc administration.

M365 Platform Governance & Administration

Own administration and platform governance of M365 foundational services, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Exchange Online, OneDrive, and related tenant-level capabilities.
Ensure M365 services are configured consistently with enterprise standards for security, retention, provisioning, lifecycle management, and service integration.
Partner with Technology Delivery to support collaboration capabilities while maintaining Cloud/Systems ownership of tenant configuration, platform controls, and technical governance.
Define guardrails for site provisioning, storage, sharing, lifecycle, service settings, and administrative ownership across M365 services.
Support data governance requirements by implementing platform-level controls for retention, classification dependencies, auditability, and access management.
Ensure M365 configuration decisions are documented, supportable, and aligned with Cybersecurity, Legal, Compliance, and business needs.

Security & Compliance Integration

Partner with Cybersecurity to ensure cloud and systems platforms meet enterprise security, data protection, and compliance expectations.
Support implementation of controls for logging, monitoring, audit readiness, vulnerability management, secure configuration, and incident response.
Ensure cloud and systems platforms align with zero trust principles and applicable frameworks such as NIST, CMMC, or other regulatory requirements.
Maintain clear ownership boundaries between Cloud/Systems platform controls, Cybersecurity policy and monitoring, and Technology Delivery business enablement. Drive remediation of platform risks related to identity, configuration drift, excessive permissions, unsupported services, and inconsistent administration practices.

Vendor, Licensing & Cloud Financial Management

Manage relationships with cloud providers, Microsoft, service partners, and key enterprise platform vendors.
Oversee cloud consumption, licensing, cost visibility, and cost optimization practices in partnership with Finance, Procurement, and technology leadership.
Establish FinOps-aligned practices for cost accountability, forecasting, service usage review, and optimization of cloud and M365 investments.
Evaluate vendor capabilities, platform roadmaps, and service changes to determine practical value and risk for Southland.
Ensure contracts, licensing models, and platform decisions support scalability, reliability, compliance, and responsible cost management.

Leadership, Team Development & Governance

Build and lead a high-performing Cloud/Systems organization, including cloud engineering, systems engineering, identity, and M365 platform administration capabilities.
Establish clear roles, responsibilities, service ownership, performance expectations, and development paths for team members.
Set priorities, manage staffing and budget needs, and align team capacity with enterprise initiatives and operational commitments.
Promote a culture of accountability, standardization, automation, documentation, and continuous improvement.
Serve as a strategic advisor to Infrastructure leadership by clearly communicating risks, tradeoffs, roadmap needs, resource constraints, and business impacts.
Develop governance practices that allow the organization to move quickly while maintaining secure, reliable, and supportable platforms.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in information technology, computer science, engineering, cybersecurity, or a related field.
10+ years of experience in cloud infrastructure, systems engineering, enterprise infrastructure, or related technology leadership roles.
5+ years of experience leading technical teams, including responsibility for planning, staffing, performance management, budgeting, and prioritization of work.
Strong experience with Microsoft Azure, M365, Entra ID, and cloud-first enterprise platform operations.
Deep understanding of identity and access management, including authentication, RBAC, conditional access, privileged access, group strategy, and identity lifecycle processes.
Experience designing and operating scalable cloud environments that support distributed companies, rapid growth, multiple offices, and diverse business needs.
Strong understanding of cloud operations, monitoring, incident response, change management, lifecycle management, backup/recovery, and service reliability practices.
Experience with infrastructure automation and infrastructure-as-code tools such as Terraform, Bicep, PowerShell, Microsoft Graph, or similar platforms.
Strong understanding of M365 platform governance, including SharePoint Online, Teams, Exchange Online, OneDrive, tenant settings, provisioning controls, retention, and platform lifecycle management.
Ability to partner effectively with Cybersecurity on zero trust, logging, secure configuration, vulnerability remediation, compliance readiness, and audit support.
Ability to work across Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Technology Delivery, Support, business teams, vendors, and executive stakeholders to align technology decisions with business priorities.
Strong communication, listening, problem-solving, and decision-making skills; ability to explain complex technical topics clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Experience managing vendor relationships, cloud consumption, licensing, and cost optimization is preferred.
Knowledge of regulatory or security frameworks such as NIST, CMMC, CIS, or similar frameworks is preferred.
Relevant certifications such as Azure Solutions Architect, Microsoft 365, CISSP, or equivalent experience are preferred.
Experience in construction or similarly distributed industries is preferred.
Willingness to travel as needed to support offices, project locations, leadership meetings, and enterprise initiatives; travel may account for up to 25% of time depending on business needs.

jobs.title: Director of Health Informatics and Technology
jobs.description:
At the University of Denver, Student Affairs is at the heart of the student journey—empowering every student to thrive academically, personally, and professionally. Rooted in DU’s signature 4D Experience, our division is committed to fostering holistic development through four dimensions: deepen intellect, develop wellbeing, discover character, and design careers and lives of purpose.

Our work reaches far beyond the classroom. Through dynamic, high-impact programs, services, and experiences offered at both the Denver Campus and the Kennedy Mountain Campus, we foster inclusive communities, promote health and wellness, cultivate exploration, engagement, and leadership, and develop a deep sense of belonging. We are committed to creating a high-touch environment where students and participants connect meaningfully, grow confidently, and thrive personally and collectively.

As a division, we serve the broader DU and Denver community which includes: Current DU Students & Families, Prospective Students & Families, Faculty & Staff, Alumni & Donors, Local Community, Companies & Organizations, and National Peers & Media. Together, we are shaping a vibrant, supportive, and dynamic campus culture where every student and participant can discover their potential and make a meaningful impact.

The Student Affairs Division Includes The Following Units

DSA Administration: 4D Experience, Office of External Relations (OER), Budget and Planning, Special Projects
Student Engagement & Leadership Development: New Student & Family Programs, 1st@DU & Pre-orientation, Post-traditional &
Student Veteran Success, Student Leadership & Service, Student Activities and Involvement, Student Center Operations
Office of the Dean of Students (DOS): Learning Effectiveness Program, Student Disability Services, Student Outreach & Support,
Student Rights & Responsibilities
Housing & Residential Education (HRE): Housing, Residential Education, Dining Services
Health & Counseling Center (HCC): Medical, Counseling, CAPE
Kennedy Mountain Campus (KMC)
Recreation and Wellness: DU Outdoors, Recreation, Wellness Promotion
The University of Denver Health & Counseling Center

Position Summary

The Director of Health Informatics and Technology serves as a critical leader and hands-on expert within the University of Denver’s Health and Counseling Center (HCC). This position blends strategic vision with operational execution, overseeing all technology systems that support the clinical, administrative, and compliance functions of the HCC. This position owns end-to-end execution of IT-related functions within the HCC.

This position summary is not designed to capture all activities, duties, or responsibilities required for this position. Responsibilities may change, or new ones may be assigned at any time.

Essential Functions

The Director provides direct support to clinical staff, ensuring timely resolution of technical issues, and leads the management of the electronic health record (EHR) system (Point and Click), server infrastructure, and security protocols. This role is responsible for developing and enforcing HIPAA-compliant IT policies, overseeing clinical coding and billing systems, and facilitating data-driven decision-making through reporting and performance analytics.

In addition to managing day-to-day IT operations, the Director partners with senior leadership to align technology strategies with the center’s evolving needs—supporting a shift toward a more efficient, private-practice-style healthcare model. The Director works collaboratively across departments to implement third-party billing systems, enhance clinical workflows, and support university-wide wellness initiatives. The role also leads administration of the National College Health Assessment (NCHA) and contributes to the development of health promotion efforts based on student needs.

The ideal candidate is a versatile and proactive leader, equally skilled at strategic planning and front-line technical support, with deep knowledge of healthcare IT, compliance, and operations in a university or clinical setting.

Reports to the Assistant Vice Chancellor of Health and Wellness and supervises the Associate Director of Information and Systems.

Knowledge

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

In-depth knowledge of Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems, preferably Point and Click or similar platforms.
Understanding HIPAA compliance and healthcare IT security standards, with the ability to implement and maintain privacy and security protocols.
Knowledge of healthcare IT infrastructure, including server management, backup systems, and patch management.
Familiarity with coding standards (e.g., CPT, ICD-10) and documentation best practices, particularly in clinical settings.
Understanding clinical billing processes and the role of third-party billing systems.
Experience with student health surveys, including NCHA (National College Health Assessment) administration and data interpretation.
Knowledge of healthcare technology trends and best practices for data-driven decision-making in healthcare.

Skills

Strong leadership and supervisory skills, with the ability to manage and mentor IT staff and other personnel.
Problem-solving skills for troubleshooting technical issues across hardware, software, and clinical systems.
Proficiency in developing and enforcing HIPAA-compliant IT policies and ensuring regular system audits for security compliance.
Ability to oversee the administration of clinical coding systems, ensuring alignment with third-party billing requirements.
Strong project management skills with the ability to prioritize multiple concurrent projects in a dynamic, service-driven environment.
Communication skills to explain technical issues to non-technical audiences, particularly clinical and administrative teams.
Proficient in data analysis and creating performance reports based on clinical data, ensuring they are accurate and timely.
Ability to collaborate across departments to improve clinical workflows and patient care processes.

Abilities

Ability to implement and support systems for tracking and analyzing clinical performance metrics.
Ability to collaborate and lead change initiatives in a healthcare setting, particularly in transforming operations into a private-practice model.
Skilled in the administration of patient clinical video systems, ensuring compliance with privacy and security regulations.
Capable of leading the procurement and lifecycle management of IT assets, ensuring all technology and infrastructure is up to date.
Ability to coordinate cross-functional projects, especially in technology and wellness initiatives, and manage stakeholder engagement.
Ability to develop and execute strategic technology plans that align with university health goals, while ensuring IT operations meet the center’s evolving needs.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in information technology, Health Informatics, Computer Science, or related field.
5+ years of professional experience in IT system management, with at least 2 years in a healthcare or clinical environment.
Demonstrated experience managing and supporting Electronic Health Record (EHR) systems, preferably Point and Click or a comparable platform.
Strong knowledge of HIPAA compliance, healthcare IT security standards, and related federal privacy regulations.
Experience supervising IT personnel, with proven ability to provide mentorship and performance oversight.
Proficiency in server administration, including backups, patch management, and security protocols.
Proven ability to troubleshoot and resolve hardware and software issues across clinical and administrative environments.
Experience in managing coding systems and aligning clinical documentation with third-party billing requirements.
Excellent communication and customer service skills, particularly in translating technical issues for non-technical audiences.
Ability to handle multiple concurrent projects in a fast-paced, service-driven environment.

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in Health Informatics, Information Systems, or a related discipline.
Experience with Point and Click EHR specifically, including configuration, user training, and integration.
Familiarity with coding standards (e.g., CPT, ICD-10) and best practices for documentation and audit-readiness in college health settings.
Experience leading technology change initiatives or digital transformation projects in healthcare or university-based clinics.
Knowledge of or experience with student health survey administration (e.g., NCHA) and using results to drive strategic health programming.
Experience with clinical video systems and managing recording and security protocols in patient care settings.
Familiarity with lab order systems and integration of diagnostic/lab workflows into EHR platforms.
Experience working in a higher education or college health environment, understanding the intersection of IT, student health, and academic priorities.
Demonstrated success in grant writing or IT resource development for health innovation projects.

Working Environment

This position requires employees to work onsite 8:00am-5:00pm M-F with occasional evening, weekends, and holiday shifts. Staff are expected to support student Hallmark, Tradition and other program events throughout the year. The University of Denver and Student Affairs recognize the utilization of flexible work arrangements where these arrangements are operationally appropriate, and supervisor approved.

Standard office environment, unexpected interruptions occur often, and stress level is moderate to high, noise level is quiet to moderate.

Physical Activities

Ability to work in front of a computer for extended periods of time.
Occasionally required to move about the office/campus.

Work Schedule

Monday - Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m.

Application Deadline

For consideration, please submit your application materials by 4:00 p.m. (MST) August 26, 2026.

Special Instructions

Candidates must apply online through jobs.du.edu to be considered. Only applications submitted online will be accepted.

Salary Grade Number

The salary grade for the position is 14.

Salary Rate

The salary rate for this position is $115,000.

The University of Denver has provided a compensation range that represents its good faith estimate of what the University may pay for the position at the time of posting. The University may ultimately pay more or less than the posted compensation range. The salary offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors such as the qualifications of the selected candidate, departmental budget availability, internal salary equity considerations, and available market information, but not based on a candidate’s sex or any other protected status.

Benefits

The University of Denver offers excellent benefits, including medical, dental, retirement, paid time off, tuition benefit and ECO pass. The University of Denver is a private institution that empowers students who want to make a difference. Learn more about the University of Denver.

jobs.title: Senior Director of Enterprise Data Partners (EDP) – Finance - Digital and Technology Partners - Hybrid
jobs.description:
Description

The Senior Director of Enterprise Data Partners (EDP) – Finance provides strategic and operational leadership for the development, governance, and delivery of enterprise data and analytics products supporting revenue cycle, finance strategy, and accounting across the Mount Sinai Health System.

Operating within a center-led, data product model, this role oversees multidisciplinary teams of data product managers, data analysts, and developers/data science analysts for delivering trusted data products including dashboards, reporting, predictive analytics, and self-service capabilities that improve financial performance and operational decision-making for the enterprise.

The Senior Director serves as the primary data and analytics partner to executive finance leadership, working collaboratively with business owners, data engineering, epic teams, digital and AI, and other DTP teams to ensure seamless product delivery and implementation. They are responsible for development of the data strategy, establishing product roadmaps, and ensuring the delivery of scalable data products in partnership with finance teams while promoting standardization, governance, Agile delivery, and measurable business outcomes.

Responsibilities

Define and execute the enterprise data product strategy for finance (revenue cycle, finance strategy, accounting), aligning initiatives to health system priorities and measurable business outcomes.
Own and scale a portfolio of enterprise data products and sources of truth, including datasets, semantic layers, dashboards, and benchmarking-integrated assets, with accountability for product vision, adoption, standardization, governance, and measurable impact on financial and operational outcomes and business value.
Partner with Finance executives to translate strategic priorities into data product roadmaps and clear delivery timelines.
Lead the transition to a product-based, agile operating model, embedding cross-functional teamwork, lifecycle accountability, and iterative delivery to drive value.
Oversee integration and optimization of internal and external data assets, including EMR, claims, and benchmarking data, enabling longitudinal and cross-continuum analytics.
Drive adoption of advanced analytics and AI-enabled capabilities that support proactive operational decision-making.
Standardize and govern enterprise metric definitions, data models, and analytics assets, reducing fragmentation, eliminating duplication, and strengthening data quality and trust in partnership with the Director of Data Governance.
Collaborate across Enterprise Data Partner leadership to enhance data architecture, optimize pipelines, and support enterprise analytics infrastructure.
Serve as a strategic advisor to executive leadership, guiding enterprise analytics investments, benchmarking strategy, and opportunities to improve quality and outcomes.
Drive enterprise adoption, enablement, and value realization of data products, ensuring alignment to measurable performance improvement and system-wide priorities.
Recruit, mentor, and lead a high-performing, multidisciplinary team, fostering a product-oriented culture of innovation, accountability, agility, and continuous improvement.
Ensure compliance with all applicable regulatory, privacy, security, and governance requirements, including HIPAA and clinical data standards.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Biostatistics, Health Informatics, Computer/Data Science, or a related field required.
Master’s or Doctoral degree preferred (e.g., MBA, MHA, MS in Data Science, PhD, MD with finance/analytics experience).
Background or certification in healthcare quality, informatics, or data science is highly desirable.

Experience Requirements

15 years of progressive information systems management experience preferably in a health care field.

Other Experience Specific To Position

10–15 years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare quality reporting and data science, with at least 5 years in finance or revenue cycle analytics for an academic health system or teaching hospital.
Demonstrated success managing teams in a multi-mission environment (clinical, operational, finance, academic).
Demonstrated success leading enterprise-scale analytics or data product organizations with accountability for domain strategy, adoption, and business outcomes.
Familiarity with AI/ML applications in healthcare analytics and decision support.
Expertise in healthcare finance and related software, data, and tools.
Familiarity with Epic or other EMRs, healthcare data warehousing, and academic research collaboration platforms.

Employer Description

Strength through Unity and Inclusion

The Mount Sinai Health System is committed to fostering an environment where everyone can contribute to excellence. We share a common dedication to delivering outstanding patient care. When you join us, you become part of Mount Sinai’s unparalleled legacy of achievement, education, and innovation as we work together to transform healthcare. We encourage all team members to actively participate in creating a culture that ensures fair access to opportunities, promotes inclusive practices, and supports the success of every individual.

At Mount Sinai, our leaders are committed to fostering a workplace where all employees feel valued, respected, and empowered to grow. We strive to create an environment where collaboration, fairness, and continuous learning drive positive change, improving the well-being of our staff, patients, and organization. Our leaders are expected to challenge outdated practices, promote a culture of respect, and work toward meaningful improvements that enhance patient care and workplace experiences. We are dedicated to building a supportive and welcoming environment where everyone has the opportunity to thrive and advance professionally. Explore this opportunity and be part of the next chapter in our history.

About The Mount Sinai Health System

Mount Sinai Health System is one of the largest academic medical systems in the New York metro area, with more than 48,000 employees working across eight hospitals, more than 400 outpatient practices, more than 300 labs, a school of nursing, and a leading school of medicine and graduate education. Mount Sinai advances health for all people, everywhere, by taking on the most complex health care challenges of our time — discovering and applying new scientific learning and knowledge; developing safer, more effective treatments; educating the next generation of medical leaders and innovators; and supporting local communities by delivering high-quality care to all who need it. Through the integration of its hospitals, labs, and schools, Mount Sinai offers comprehensive health care solutions from birth through geriatrics, leveraging innovative approaches such as artificial intelligence and informatics while keeping patients’ medical and emotional needs at the center of all treatment. The Health System includes more than 9,000 primary and specialty care physicians; 13 joint-venture outpatient surgery centers throughout the five boroughs of New York City, Westchester, Long Island, and Florida; and more than 30 affiliated community health centers. We are consistently ranked by U.S. News & World Report's Best Hospitals, receiving high "Honor Roll" status, and are highly ranked: No. 1 in Geriatrics, top 5 in Cardiology/Heart Surgery, and top 20 in Diabetes/Endocrinology, Gastroenterology/GI Surgery, Neurology/Neurosurgery, Orthopedics, Pulmonology/Lung Surgery, Rehabilitation, and Urology. New York Eye and Ear Infirmary of Mount Sinai is ranked No. 12 in Ophthalmology. U.S. News & World Report’s “Best Children’s Hospitals” ranks Mount Sinai Kravis Children's Hospital among the country’s best in several pediatric specialties. The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is ranked No. 11 nationwide in National Institutes of Health funding and in the 99th percentile in research dollars per investigator according to the Association of American Medical Colleges. Newsweek’s “The World’s Best Smart Hospitals” ranks The Mount Sinai Hospital as No. 1 in New York and in the top five globally, and Mount Sinai Morningside in the top 20 globally.

Equal Opportunity Employer

The Mount Sinai Health System is an equal opportunity employer, complying with all applicable federal civil rights laws. We do not discriminate, exclude, or treat individuals differently based on race, color, national origin, age, religion, disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We are deeply committed to fostering an environment where all faculty, staff, students, trainees, patients, visitors, and the communities we serve feel respected and supported. Our goal is to create a healthcare and learning institution that actively works to remove barriers, address challenges, and promote fairness in all aspects of our organization.

Compensation

The Mount Sinai Health System (MSHS) provides salary ranges that comply with the New York City Law on Salary Transparency in Job Advertisements. The salary range for the role is $183854 - $289990 Annually. Actual salaries depend on a variety of factors, including experience, education, and operational need. The salary range or contractual rate listed does not include bonuses/incentive, differential pay or other forms of compensation or benefits.

jobs.title: Director, Software Development
jobs.description:
The Director of Engineering at PowerPlan is a senior technology leader responsible for building, scaling, and operating the next generation architecture PowerPlan’s cloud-native SaaS platform modernizing a decades trusted regulated utility product suite. This role is accountable for turning strategy into execution delivering modern architecture, accelerating SaaS adoption, improving engineering productivity, and ensuring security, reliability, and compliance while maintaining the trust of utility customers who operate in highly regulated environments. This leader is hands on where it matters, deeply accountable for outcomes, and a role model for PowerPlan’s culture of ownership, clarity, and continuous improvement.

What Success Looks Like (12-24 Months)

A successful Director of Engineering will

Deliver measurable progress on NXT adoption (customer migrations, production usage, ARR contribution).
Establish a clear, scalable NXT reference architecture that teams consistently follow.
Improve engineering execution metrics (predictability, cycle time, quality, reliability).
Reduce operational noise (support tickets, manual processes, regressions).
Build a strong bench of leaders (Managers, Directors, Architects) who operate with ownership.
Be viewed by Product, Architecture, CloudOps, InfoSec, and GTM as a trusted execution partner, not a bottleneck.

Core Responsibilities

NXT Architecture & Platform Execution
Own the end-to-end delivery of the NXT engineering roadmap in partnership with Architecture and Product.
Translate architectural vision into clear, executable engineering plans with milestones, dependencies, and measurable outcomes.
Ensure consistent adoption of
Cloud-native patterns (Azure-first, microservices where appropriate)
API-first and integration standards
Data platform strategy (Databricks, analytics, reporting)
Security-by-design and compliance-ready architectures

Balance modernization speed with operational safety for regulated utility customers.

Expectation Architecture does not remain theoretical, teams ship production ready, supportable systems.

Engineering Delivery & Operational Excellence
Own engineering delivery across
New feature development
Legacy modernization
SaaS migration
Platform reliability and scalability

Establish clear ownership models for services, domains, and systems.
Improve SDLC discipline
Predictable planning and delivery
Strong definition of “done”
Reduced rework and technical debt

Partner with CloudOps and InfoSec to ensure
≥99% uptime
Secure, compliant releases
Operational readiness before customer adoption

Expectation Engineering delivers with confidence, not heroics.

Talent, Leadership & Team Health
Lead and develop Engineering Managers, Directors, and senior ICs.
Set clear expectations for
Accountability
Technical rigor
Collaboration
Decision ownership

Actively coach leaders on
Translating strategy into execution
Managing trade-offs
Giving clear feedback

Build a culture where
Problems are surfaced early
Decisions are documented
Teams feel ownership, not fear

Expectation Strong leaders create strong teams; weak ownership is addressed directly.

Cross-Functional Partnership
Work tightly with
Product - aligning engineering execution to customer and market priorities
Architecture - ensuring designs are implementable and scalable
CloudOps / SaaSOps - operational excellence and cost efficiency
InfoSec - audit-ready, compliant engineering practices
Professional Services & Support - smooth customer onboarding and reduced friction

Provide clear trade-off recommendations when priorities compete.
Represent Engineering in executive-level discussions with data, clarity, and confidence.

Expectation Engineering is seen as a business enabler, not a constraint.

Metrics, Transparency & Continuous Improvement
Own and report on engineering KPIs, including
Delivery predictability
SaaS adoption enablement
Quality and defect trends
Cloud cost efficiency per customer
Support ticket reduction

Use metrics to drive action, not just reporting.
Continuously improve processes, tooling, and developer experience.

Lead a once-in-a-generation platform transformation.
Work on mission-critical software trusted by the world’s largest utilities.
Partner with an experienced executive team focused on long-term value.
Shape the future of a growing SaaS business within a strong Roper portfolio.

Leadership & Delivery

10+ years in software engineering, with 5+ years leading large, multi-team organizations.
Proven experience modernizing enterprise SaaS platforms from legacy architectures.
Strong track record of delivering complex, multi year transformations.

Cloud platforms (Azure preferred)

Enterprise integration patterns
AI, Data platforms and analytics

Comfortable balancing speed, quality, cost, and risk.

jobs.title: Solar Director of Preconstruction and Engineering
jobs.description:
Company Overview

Moss is a national privately held construction firm providing innovative solutions resulting in award-winning projects. With regional offices across the United States, Moss focuses on construction management, solar EPC, design-build, and public-private partnerships. The company’s diverse portfolio encompasses a wide range of sectors, including luxury high-rise residential, landmark mixed-use developments, hospitality, K-12 and higher education, justice, solar energy and battery storage, and sports. Moss is ranked by Engineering News-Record as one of the nation’s top 65 general contractors, and the 3rd ranked solar EPC nationwide. Moss prides itself on a strong entrepreneurial culture that honors safety, quality, client engagement and employee development. Its employees consistently rank Moss as one of the best places to work.

POSITION SCOPE AND ORGANIZATIONAL IMPACT

The Solar Director of Preconstruction and Engineering
provides leadership for preconstruction, estimating, and engineering functions to support the Solar Division in the pursuit and execution of large utility-scale solar projects
based out of the Hawaii Office
. This role drives accuracy and consistency in estimating, oversight of engineering deliverables, team development, and collaboration with owners, consultants, trade contractors, and vendors to support successful project pursuits and transitions to operations.

Essential Job Duties And Responsibilities

Lead and manage the preconstruction and engineering effort for utility-scale solar projects, from early-stage concept through final contract pricing and handoff.
Manage the estimating process for EPC, conceptual/schematic, and various stages of progress construction drawings through final contract pricing for the solar industry.
Produce estimate summaries indicating project costs and margin potential, while supporting conversion to both Owner bid forms and Moss internal budget formats.
Prepare, update, and track estimates as design documents progress, including value engineering analysis and reconciliation of scope, assumptions, and clarifications.
Provide leadership in creating, reviewing, and revising drafts and deliverables for solar utility-scale ground mount projects.
Review, analyze, and provide comments on owner contracts, subcontract agreements, consultant agreements, and other project related contracts to identify commercial, technical, operational, and risk related issues.
Build, train, and manage the preconstruction and engineering team; establish assignments, priorities, and key staff objectives.
Provide training/seminars to the department and promote continuous improvement in estimating, engineering coordination, and preconstruction processes.
Monitor adherence to all departmental processes; correct non-compliance as required.
Conduct department meetings and ensure clear communication of expectations, schedules, and deliverables.
Responsible for all deliverables produced by the department, ensuring completeness, accuracy, and timeliness.
Support and manage relationships with owners, design consultants, vendors, and trade contractors to align with project goals.
Coordinate project handoff to operations teams and ensure all preconstruction, engineering, and contractual information is accurately transferred for successful project execution
Establish and maintain strong business relationships with trade contractors and vendors to ensure support and interest in bidding and executing solar projects.
Provide support to early-stage project management, engineering, and operations teams to enable successful project planning and execution.
Communicate and interact effectively with the project owner, design consultants, and Moss staff to meet project goals.
Provide high-level summaries of bids to the Leadership Team at the time of submission or by the following morning, including key risks, assumptions, and opportunities.
Focus on risk management training and development of systems, standards, constructability, and scope development practices.
Oversee trade contractor compliance and performance expectations (including contractor scorecards) for trade contractors bidding projects.
Review trade contractor applicants who submit information through established channels and/or advise the Vice President of Solar as appropriate.
Provide staff performance reviews and recommend salary adjustments to the Vice President of Solar.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Education And Work Experience

Bachelor’s degree in construction management, civil engineering, electrical engineering, or related discipline preferred.
Minimum 8 years of engineering and management experience, including minimum 5 years supporting utility-scale solar projects.
Strong background in solar utility-scale ground mount projects (engineering coordination, constructability, and preconstruction execution).
Strong estimating and project scheduling background.
Strong computer skills are a necessity (MS Office / Excel / PowerPoint / Word), including familiarity with construction project management applications and estimating software.
Experience with HCSS Heavy Bid, Accubid, MS Project, Primavera, AGTEK, BlueBeam, and InSite Software is an advantage.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills required to interface directly with owners’ representatives, the A/E team, building departments, and other team members.
Ability to read, interpret, and understand plans proficiently; ability to read specifications and understand subject matter.
Ability to perform accurate quantity survey take-offs.
Demonstrated leadership skills, including experience managing and developing teams of estimators, project engineers, and/or engineering staff.
