jobs.description:
About Us

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.

The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.

Role Summary

We are looking for a Director of Data to own our data strategy and platform as we scale toward software-defined vehicles.

This is a hands-on leadership role where you'll set technical direction and stay close to the architecture and code, while building and managing a high-performing team responsible for high-volume, high-velocity vehicle and enterprise data.

You'll bring both the technical depth to make sound platform decisions and the people leadership to grow and run a team operating at scale.

We're hiring for this role in Palo Alto, Irvine, or Vancouver. We are happy to work with whichever location suits you best.

Responsibilities

Define and drive the data strategy and roadmap across vehicle telemetry, manufacturing, and enterprise data domains, aligning with engineering, product, and business stakeholders.
Own architecture decisions for large-scale data platforms (ingestion, storage, processing, and serving layers) handling high-volume streaming and batch data.
Stay hands-on: review designs and code, dive into pipeline or performance issues, and set technical standards by example, not just by policy.
Recruit, manage, mentor, and grow a team of data engineers and analytics professionals; own hiring plans, performance management, and career development.
Partner with quality, manufacturing, product, and software engineering teams to ensure data infrastructure supports reliability, safety, and product analytics needs.
Establish data governance, quality, and security standards across pipelines and platforms, ensuring compliance with relevant regulatory and privacy requirements.
Build and maintain stakeholder-facing reporting on platform health, data quality, and delivery against roadmap commitments.
Evaluate and integrate modern tooling (e.g., Databricks, Spark, Kafka, cloud data warehouses, AI/LLM-assisted engineering tools) to keep the platform and team ahead of scale demands.
Manage budget, vendor, and tooling decisions for the data organization.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:

8–10 years of overall industry experience in data engineering or analytics, including 3+ years managing high-volume data engineering or analytics teams.
Demonstrated hands-on technical depth in building and operating large-scale data systems, proficiency in SQL and Python required, along with hands-on experience with Databricks required (additional experience with Spark or equivalent distributed data platforms a plus).
Track record of designing and scaling data architecture (ingestion, ETL/ELT, streaming, and storage) for high-volume, high-velocity data.
Experience hiring, developing, and retaining data engineering talent, with a demonstrated ability to balance IC-level technical involvement with people leadership.
Strong cross-functional partnership skills and being comfortable working with engineering, product, quality, and manufacturing stakeholders to translate business needs into data infrastructure.
Experience establishing data governance, quality, and security practices at an organizational level.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline; advanced degree a plus.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in automotive, mobility, IoT, or another industry with high-volume sensor/telemetry data.
Experience integrating or prompting AI/LLM tools into engineering workflows.
Familiarity with dashboard/BI tooling (HEX, Tableau, Power BI, or similar) for stakeholder reporting.

Total Rewards

We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program.

Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. This role is also eligible for equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), subject to board approval and the terms of our equity incentive plans, including applicable vesting requirements.

In addition to our compensation programs, we invest in our people with a comprehensive benefits package designed to support the health, wellbeing, and financial future for full-time employees — including health coverage, retirement savings, time off, and family planning programs. About the role:

Serve as Portsmouth Power owner technical authority. This role owns the technical basis, owner requirements, design assurance, technology/configuration evaluation, engineering interfaces, utility/interconnection technical coordination, constructability input, and technical readiness for procurement, permitting, execution, commissioning, and operations readiness.

Office Location:
We are hiring for this position in NY and CA and are also open to candidates located in Ohio or Texas. Compensation may vary depending on geographic location, experience, and other job-related factors.

What success looks like in the first 6-12 months

Owner technical requirements, basis of design, design review process, and technical decision log established and controlled.
Power generation architecture, BOP, electrical interconnection, gas/fuel, water, emissions, site layout, commissioning assumptions, and tenant interface requirements integrated into a coherent technical basis.
Owner Engineer, PMO, EPC/EPCM, OEM, utility, and consultant engineering scopes clearly aligned with DOR/RACI and deliverable expectations.
Long-lead equipment technical requirements and bid evaluation criteria established for procurement decisions.
Technical risks surfaced early with clear implications for cost, schedule, permits, commercial commitments, and execution readiness.

Key responsibilities

Own the owner-side technical strategy and technical governance framework for Portsmouth Power, including basis of design, owner requirements, technical specifications, design review protocols, and technical decision rights.
Lead technical evaluation of power generation configurations, balance-of-plant, electrical interconnection, switchyard/substation, transmission interface, gas/fuel supply interface, water/wastewater, emissions, controls, and commissioning requirements.
Manage Owner Engineer and technical consultants to ensure deliverables are fit-for-purpose, decision-ready, and aligned with program schedule and procurement needs.
Review and challenge PMO, EPC/EPCM, OEM, and consultant technical assumptions, design deliverables, studies, specifications, engineering schedules, and procurement packages.
Support technology and OEM due diligence, including gas turbine/major equipment selection, constructability, operability, maintainability, performance, availability, emissions, lifecycle cost, and supply chain implications.

Partner with Program Delivery and Program Controls to ensure design maturity, engineering deliverables, permitting dependencies, interconnection milestones, and commissioning assumptions are reflected in the integrated master schedule.
Coordinate technical interfaces with utilities, RTO/interconnection stakeholders, gas/fuel providers, site/infrastructure teams, tenants/customers, permitting consultants, and regulatory stakeholders.
Establish design assurance, value engineering, constructability review, management of change, and technical risk processes without slowing decision velocity unnecessarily.
Build future engineering and technical capability as the program matures, including discipline engineering, commissioning/ops readiness technical input, QA/QC, and document control interfaces.
Travel as required.

Key interfaces

GM, Program Delivery/Integration, Program Controls, Commercial/Contracts/Offtake, Procurement, Gas/Fuel Supply, Permitting, Construction/Site Delivery.
Owner Engineer, PMO technical team, EPC/EPCM engineers, SoftBank Energy, OEMs, utilities, RTO/interconnection stakeholders, permitting consultants, and tenant technical teams.
SoftBank technology, finance, legal, government affairs, insurance, and executive stakeholders as needed for major technical decisions.

Required qualifications

Bachelor degree in electrical, mechanical, civil, chemical, power systems, or related engineering field.
15+ years of engineering leadership experience in power generation, energy infrastructure, utilities, transmission/substation, oil and gas, LNG/midstream, industrial infrastructure, or comparable capital-intensive projects.
Demonstrated experience supporting large capital projects from development/FEED through procurement, execution, commissioning, and operations readiness.
Deep knowledge of power generation systems, balance-of-plant, electrical interconnection, major equipment, constructability, commissioning assumptions, technical risk, and design assurance.
Experience managing Owner Engineer, Softbank Energy, EPC/EPCM, OEM, or technical consultant deliverables and holding external technical parties accountable.
Ability to translate technical issues into commercial, schedule, permitting, reliability, operability, and executive decision implications.
Strong safety, quality, technical integrity, and management of change mindset.
Strong written and verbal executive communication skills with ability to brief technical decisions clearly and concisely.

Preferred qualifications

Professional Engineer license or equivalent technical credential.
Experience with combined cycle, simple cycle, peaking generation, gas turbines, HRSGs, transformers, switchgear, substations, switchyards, transmission interconnection, and related BOP systems.
Experience with PJM, AEP, FERC, NERC, or comparable utility/RTO/interconnection processes.
Experience with hyperscale data center power requirements, high-reliability power systems, microgrids, energy storage, advanced cooling, or large industrial load integration.
Experience with emissions/permitting engineering, water/wastewater constraints, gas supply interfaces, and technology down-select decisions.
Advanced degree in engineering, energy systems, business, or project management.

Leadership attributes

Technical authority with commercial judgment: rigorous but practical.
Decision-oriented: creates clarity and recommendations, not endless study cycles.
Constructability-minded: knows that design quality is measured by field execution and operations outcomes.
Strong interface leader: can align engineering, procurement, commercial, permitting, construction, and tenant requirements.
Calm under pressure: credible in technical debates with OEMs, utilities, contractors, and executives.

Who We Are

Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.

The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.

Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.

What We Value

We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy.

We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach.

Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

Seek Excellence.
Be Selective To Be Effective.
Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
Disagree Transparently.
Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
Build Dream Teams.

Who You Are

A collaborative and strategic leader with deep hands-on experience in Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) and infrastructure Automation.

You are comfortable steering the vision for an enterprise automation roadmap while remaining technical enough to dive into the code.

You treat infrastructure as a product, ensuring that your automation workflows are as reliable as the services they deploy.

You have a proven track record of managing complex hybrid environments and are proactive in building self-service platforms that enhance engineering velocity and system stability.

Responsibilities

Automation Platform Leadership: Oversee a specialized SRE team focused on the design, deployment, and maintenance of automation toolsets as well as the systems they interact with.
Infrastructure as Code (IaC) Governance: Establish and enforce standards for IaC to ensure consistent, repeatable, and secure deployments across an entire infrastructure ecosystem. Strong proficiency in Terraform is required.
Configuration Management: Lead the strategy for automated configuration and state management, ensuring Ansible playbooks and Packer image pipelines are optimized for both Windows, Linux, and ESXi Platforms.
Monitoring & Observability: Manage the monitoring and health of the automation platforms themselves. Implement SLIs/SLOs to ensure the "tools that build the servers" are highly available and performant.
Lifecycle Management: Drive the automated lifecycle of both physical and virtual assets, from initial template creation/deployment to automated patching, scaling, and decommissioning.
Custom Tooling & Scripting: Lead the development of custom scripts and internal providers (Python, Go, PowerShell, Bash) to provide better insights and tooling for our systems.
Collaboration: Outside of the automation team you will need to be able to collaborate and foster workflows alongside the rest of the Datacenter team and be able to facilitate needs for the team as a whole.
Capacity & Performance: Analyze system behavior and resource utilization in virtual environments to optimize the performance of automated deployments.
Mentorship & Growth: Provide technical guidance and career mentorship to SREs, fostering a culture of "automate-first" and continuous improvement.

Requirements

6-10 years’ experience in Infrastructure, SRE or DevOps, specifically focused on infrastructure automation at scale.
Deep proficiency with Terraform (providers, modules, state management) and Ansible (roles, playbooks, Tower/AWX).
Hands-on experience with Image Creation (i.e. Packer, Ansible, SCCM) to build standardized, hardened images for both Windows and Linux in hybrid environments.
Strong experience managing and automating virtual platforms such as VMware (vSphere/vCenter) as well as Cloud providers such as Azure and AWS.
High-level scripting skills in mediums such as Python, Go, PowerShell, and Bash.
Experience with observability tools (Splunk, ELK, Prometheus, or Grafana) to monitor infrastructure health and automation telemetry.
Good understanding of Network topology and design as well as experience with platforms such as Juniper Networks or Palo Alto.
Strong mastery of Git (branching strategies, PR workflows) and CI/CD platforms (Jenkins, GitLab CI, or GitHub Actions).
Equal comfort managing, troubleshooting, and tuning performance for both Windows Server and Linux.

Nice to Have

Previous work experience includes notable periods of team leadership and or management.
Experience with IAM platforms such as Entra ID, Active Directory, and Okta.
Experience with Storage solutions both block based and object based hosted either on-prem (HP Alletra, EMC, DDN) or in cloud (S3, Azure Blob).
Storage Backup/DR administration and management with Commvault or Veeam.

jobs.title: Head of Commerce Technology & Growth
jobs.description:
About This Role

At tarte, our technology team moves as quickly as our business does. We're looking for a hands-on, experienced engineer who is excited to spend time in the code, collaborate closely with our cross-functional teams, and help shape the technology behind our growing global ecommerce business.
Tarte is a founder-led brand that moves fast, stays close to our customers, and adapts when new opportunities arise. Our engineering team supports a Shopify Plus platform powering a global DTC business across 50 active markets, with an ecommerce experience that is constantly evolving through product launches, influencer activations, OMS integrations, and new AI-powered capabilities.
In this role, you'll be a key technical partner across our commerce ecosystem: writing code, defining architecture, solving complex technical challenges, and bringing thoughtful solutions to the table. You'll work directly with Product, Merchandising, Marketing, and other cross-functional partners on technical decisions that support the customer experience and drive the business forward.
What You'll Own

Hands-On Technical Expertise

Writing code is a core part of this role. You'll contribute to Shopify Plus custom apps using Liquid, Node.js, and React; own and extend AWS Lambda functions that connect our OMS to the broader commerce stack; and partner with our OMS team on backend integrations across order management, fulfillment, and downstream systems.
When complex technical challenges arise, you'll help evaluate the options, identify the right path forward, and bring others along by explaining the why behind technical decisions.
Architecture Guidance & Team Collaboration

You'll bring strong technical judgment to architecture and development decisions across the team. You'll review technical approaches, identify potential risks early, share best practices, and help build scalable solutions that support both our immediate needs and long-term growth.
You'll also be a resource for other engineers, sharing your experience through technical discussions, code reviews, and collaborative problem solving while helping the team continue to grow its technical capabilities.
Marketing & Business Partnership

You understand that great technology starts with understanding what the business is trying to accomplish. You'll work closely with Marketing, Merchandising, Product, and other teams to understand upcoming launches, initiatives, and opportunities, then help translate those needs into thoughtful technical solutions.
You're comfortable connecting technical decisions to business outcomes and communicating complex ideas in a way that is clear, practical, and actionable for both technical and non-technical partners.
Vendor Evaluations & Platform Intelligence

You'll own technical vendor evaluations, from defining criteria and conducting assessments to providing clear, thoughtful recommendations.
You'll also stay ahead of the Shopify Plus roadmap and broader ecommerce landscape, proactively identifying platform changes, new capabilities, and opportunities that could benefit tarte. Site performance, digital accessibility, and the overall customer experience will remain top of mind as you evaluate new features and functionality.
AI-First Commerce

We're actively exploring how AI can make the way we build, test, deploy, and optimize our ecommerce experiences even smarter.
You'll contribute to AI-enabled deployment workflows, GEO and LLM product discovery, automated quality gates, and other emerging applications of AI across the commerce stack. You bring a practical and curious perspective on where AI can create meaningful value and are excited to experiment, learn, and help turn new ideas into real-world solutions.
What You Bring

What We're Looking For:

7+ years of ecommerce engineering experience with strong, hands-on Shopify Plus experience, including Liquid, Shopify APIs, custom apps, Checkout Extensibility, Shopify Flow, metafields, and multi-market configuration
Hands-on experience with AWS Lambda or equivalent serverless technologies, including building, troubleshooting, and maintaining functions
Experience architecting integrations across the commerce ecosystem, including ERP, OMS, CRM, payments, and fulfillment
Ability to clearly communicate technical architecture and decisions to both technical and non-technical partners
Experience mentoring and collaborating with other engineers and sharing technical knowledge across a team
Comfortable owning vendor evaluations, including setting criteria, assessing technical capabilities, and providing recommendations
Flexible and adaptable in your approach, with the ability to respond to changing priorities and feedback
A solutions-oriented mindset: when the original request isn't technically feasible, you look for creative and practical alternatives

Additional Technical Skills:

JavaScript / TypeScript, React, and Node.js
GraphQL, REST APIs, and webhook-based integrations
CI/CD pipelines, Git workflows, and automated testing
Web performance fundamentals, including Core Web Vitals, page speed, and third-party script management
Hands-on experience using Postman to troubleshoot, validate, and diagnose API behavior, including authentication, request/response payloads, environment configuration, and error handling

What Will Make You Stand Out:

Experience with GEO, LLM-based product discovery, or AI tooling within an ecommerce environment
Experience working within founder-led, DTC, beauty, fashion, or lifestyle brands
An understanding of what it takes to succeed in a fast-moving consumer brand where priorities can evolve quickly
Curiosity about emerging ecommerce technologies and a desire to continuously test, learn, and improve
The ability to balance technical depth with a strong understanding of the customer and the business

Our Culture

Tarte is a global beauty brand with the energy and entrepreneurial spirit of a founder-led business. We move quickly, think creatively, and stay close to our customers. Our teams are collaborative, curious, and commercially minded, with a shared focus on creating great experiences and driving the business forward.
Our roadmap is always evolving, and priorities can shift as new opportunities emerge. We value people who are comfortable with change, communicate openly, and enjoy solving problems together.
You're someone who can take an idea or business need, ask thoughtful questions, collaborate with the right partners, and turn it into a solution that works. You're excited by an environment where you can be hands-on, have an impact, and see your work come to life across a global ecommerce platform.
This role is hybrid and based in New York City, with two days per week in office required.
Our Perks

Salary range: $130,000-150,000 (Compensation will depend on a variety of factors, including but not limited to skill level, relevant work experience & education)
Medical, dental, vision, 401K plan & access to health & wellness programs
Paid vacation, holidays, summer Fridays, birthdays off, volunteer time & more

Director of Information Technology

Position Summary

The Director of Information Technology will take ownership of an established technology environment and lead the next phase of its evolution. Reporting directly to the CEO, this leader will be responsible for improving technology reliability, strengthening cybersecurity, simplifying systems, enhancing the end-user experience, and ensuring technology effectively supports exceptional patient care and operational performance.
This is an ideal opportunity for a strong IT Manager, Senior Manager, or emerging Director who is ready to broaden their leadership scope. The Director will work closely with executive, clinical, and operational leaders; manage key technology partners; oversee the EMR function; and lead practical, high-impact initiatives across a growing healthcare platform.
The successful candidate will be analytical, hands-on, service-oriented, and energized by the opportunity to make visible improvements in an environment where technology directly impacts clinicians, staff, patients, and organizational growth.

Key Responsibilities

Optimize and Strengthen the Technology Environment

Assess current systems, infrastructure, support processes, and technology spend to identify opportunities to improve performance, consistency, efficiency, and end-user experience.
Lead initiatives that enhance the reliability and usability of clinic hardware, networking, communications, and core business systems.
Drive practical standardization across locations while preserving appropriate flexibility for clinical and operational requirements.
Support strategic initiatives such as VoIP centralization, hardware refreshes, connectivity improvements, and consolidation of overlapping technology platforms.
Establish clear technology standards, documentation, processes, and operating rhythms that improve efficiency and scalability as the organization grows.

Vendor & Technology Partner Oversight

Serve as the primary internal leader for outsourced IT providers, managed service providers, and technology vendors.
Hold external partners accountable for service expectations, responsiveness, cybersecurity requirements, and measurable business outcomes.
Identify opportunities to simplify the technology vendor ecosystem, improve service quality, and maximize the value of existing technology investments.
Participate in vendor evaluations, contract negotiations and renewals, service-level discussions, and performance reviews in partnership with executive leadership.
Build productive, collaborative, and accountable relationships with internal stakeholders and external technology partners.

Advance Cybersecurity & Compliance

Strengthen cybersecurity practices, data protection, technology governance, and risk management across the organization.
Maintain and improve HIPAA-aligned controls, user access practices, backup and disaster-recovery processes, and incident-response readiness.
Monitor technology risks and coordinate practical remediation plans with internal leaders, managed service providers, and external cybersecurity experts.
Promote a culture in which security, privacy, and responsible technology use are integrated into everyday operations.
Help ensure technology practices and controls appropriately support the organization's regulatory and compliance obligations.

Manage Applications & EMR Platform

Oversee and support the EMR Manager and EMR Specialist in maintaining and advancing a consistent, high-performing clinical technology environment.
Partner with clinical, revenue cycle, and operations leaders to improve workflows within the EMR and practice-management ecosystem.
Support the integration of acquired and new clinics into existing systems, technology standards, processes, and support models.
Ensure EMR priorities are aligned with broader infrastructure, cybersecurity, compliance, and operational objectives.
Identify opportunities to leverage technology to improve clinical workflows, staff productivity, patient experience, and organizational performance.

Deliver High-Impact Technology Projects

Lead technology projects from planning through implementation, establishing clear ownership, timelines, communication plans, and measurable outcomes.
Translate operational and business challenges into pragmatic, scalable technology solutions.
Establish and track meaningful KPIs related to service levels, project delivery, system performance, vendor performance, cybersecurity, and technology investments.
Communicate project progress, risks, opportunities, and recommendations clearly and effectively to the CEO and leadership team.
Ensure projects are delivered with appropriate change management, stakeholder engagement, and follow-through.

Grow as a Strategic Technology Leader

Partner directly with the CEO and senior leadership team to establish technology priorities that support organizational growth, performance, and scalability.
Develop into a trusted cross-functional leader who understands the connection between technology, clinical operations, patient experience, financial performance, and business growth.
Lead, mentor, and develop internal IT and EMR team members while creating a culture of responsiveness, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
Balance strategic thinking with a willingness to engage directly in solving important technology and operational problems.
Continuously evaluate emerging technologies and industry practices for their potential to improve the organization's operations and competitive position.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field required.
5–8+ years of progressive IT experience, including meaningful responsibility for infrastructure, systems, vendors, technology projects, cybersecurity, or end-user support.
Prior management, team-lead, or significant cross-functional leadership experience preferred.
Experience in healthcare, multi-site operations, professional services, or another complex service environment preferred.
Experience working with managed service providers, technology vendors, or outsourced IT teams strongly preferred.
Experience supporting an EMR, practice-management system, or other healthcare application environment is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Strong foundation in IT infrastructure, end-user technology, networking, cybersecurity, cloud-based business systems, and technology operations.
Ability to assess existing processes and systems, identify the highest-value opportunities for improvement, and execute with discipline.
Strong project-management skills, including prioritization, organization, follow-through, communication, and accountability.
Demonstrated ability to manage vendors, evaluate performance, resolve service issues, and advocate for practical, cost-effective solutions.
Interest in healthcare technology, privacy, compliance, and the ways technology can improve clinical and operational workflows.
Sound judgment, intellectual curiosity, problem-solving ability, and a bias toward action.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to build credibility and strong working relationships with clinicians, staff, executives, vendors, and external partners.
Ability to balance strategic priorities with hands-on problem solving in a growing organization.
Growth mindset and demonstrated ambition to take on increasing leadership responsibility over time.

Position Summary

The Director of Innovation leads TPI's technology development function, driving the creation and maturation of new and emerging technologies for composite wind blade design, materials, and manufacturing. This role owns the full technology pipeline — from early-stage concept and low Technology Readiness Level (TRL) research through TRL 8/9 qualification and Manufacturing Readiness Level (MRL) 6 production implementation — while also scouting, evaluating, and deploying existing external technologies and solutions with applicability to TPI's production process. The Director builds and leads a team of engineers and technologists, sets the technology roadmap, and partners closely with engineering, operations, quality, and program management to convert innovation into measurable production impact.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Lead, build, and develop a team responsible for the development of new and low-TRL technologies across materials, processes, tooling, and automation for composite wind blade manufacturing.
Own technology maturation from concept through TRL 8/9 and MRL 6, establishing and managing stage-gate processes, milestones, and go/no-go criteria for each development program.
Identify, evaluate, and vet existing technologies and solutions (internal or external to TPI) for applicability and transferability to current production processes; lead build-vs-buy-vs-partner assessments.
Establish and maintain a technology roadmap aligned with business strategy, customer requirements, and manufacturing capability needs.
Champion the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning methods to accelerate technology development, modeling, process optimization, and decision-making.
Direct experimental design, testing, characterization, and numerical/physical modeling required to validate new technologies prior to production release.
Partner with Advanced Manufacting, engineering, operations, quality, and program management to plan and execute technology transitions into serial production with minimal risk.
Manage technology development budgets, timelines, resourcing, and external partnerships (universities, suppliers, national labs, technology vendors).
Build and protect TPI's intellectual property portfolio through disciplined invention disclosure, patent strategy, and technical documentation.
Develop business cases, cost-benefit analyses, and ROI models to prioritize and justify technology investments to senior leadership.
Mentor and develop engineering and technical staff, growing organizational capability in technology development, AI application, and composites manufacturing.
Represent TPI's technology function with customers, suppliers, industry groups, and at technical conferences.
Perform other related duties and special projects as assigned.

Required Qualifications (Education, Skills, and Experience)

Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Materials, Aerospace, or Manufacturing Engineering, or a related technical field required; advanced degree preferred.
Minimum 10-15 years of progressive experience in technology/product development, R&D, or advanced manufacturing engineering, including significant experience leading technical teams or programs.
Demonstrated experience taking technologies through formal TRL/MRL (or equivalent stage-gate) maturation processes from concept to production.
Required AI literacy: demonstrated hands-on experience applying artificial intelligence and/or machine learning tools and techniques to engineering, R&D, or manufacturing problems, and working knowledge of how AI can be applied to accelerate technology development.
Strong background in composites, materials science, or advanced manufacturing processes; wind blade or wind energy industry experience strongly preferred.
Proven ability to scout, assess, and integrate third-party or existing technologies into an operating production environment.
Experience with numerical modeling, simulation, CAE/FEA tools, and experimental test design and characterization.
Strong leadership, team-building, and people-development skills, with experience managing engineers and technologists.
Ability to build and present business cases, technology roadmaps, and budget justifications to executive leadership.
Excellent verbal and written communication and interpersonal skills; verbal and written fluency in English.
Strong critical thinking, problem analysis, and hands-on, practical problem-solving abilities.
Ability to work effectively across a distributed, global organization and with cross-functional/multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's degree or Ph.D. in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
Direct experience in wind blade design, composites manufacturing, or renewable energy technology development.
Track record of patents, publications, or other intellectual property contributions.
Experience developing or deploying custom AI/ML models (e.g., predictive modeling, computer vision for defect detection, process optimization algorithms).
Formal program/project management training or certification (e.g., PMP).
Experience managing external partnerships with universities, national labs, or technology suppliers.
Familiarity with CAD/CAM and simulation tools such as ABAQUS or CATIA.

This position requires approximately 25-50% travel, depending on project needs, including visits to TPI manufacturing facilities, supplier and technology partner sites, testing facilities, and industry conferences. Travel may include both domestic and international destinations.

The Data Engineering team at Imprint builds the foundation that enables teams and systems across the company to understand, trust, and use data. We own the core data platform, development patterns, and standards behind Imprint's enterprise data warehouse, partnering closely with Infrastructure and with teams across the business.

As Imprint scales, one of our biggest data challenges is turning an increasingly complex business into data that is consistent, understandable, and easy to use by machines or people. Doing that well requires great analytics engineering: clear models of the business, strong definitions and abstractions, and systems that make high-quality data development repeatable.

We don't believe the answer is simply adding more Data Engineers. We want to build a platform that gives domain experts across Imprint the tools and guardrails to contribute safely and independently—allowing us to dramatically increase the pace of analytics engineering without making Data Engineering a bottleneck.

We're looking for a Data Engineering Senior Manager
to lead this next phase of our Data Engineering organization. You will build and develop a high-performing team, raise the bar for analytics engineering, and create the platform and development model that allow high-quality data development to scale across Imprint.

This is a people leadership role for someone with deep technical judgment. You won't carry an individual contributor roadmap, but you should be comfortable getting into the details, challenging assumptions, and helping the team reason from first principles about data modeling, architecture, and engineering practices.

What You'll Do

Build and lead an exceptional Data Engineering team. Hire great engineers, coach and develop the team, grow senior technical leaders, set a high performance bar, and create a culture of ownership and continuous improvement.
Use AI to increase both speed and quality. Develop and implement a point of view on how AI can improve the full analytics engineering lifecycle, from stakeholder engagement, team management, to design and development.
Set the technical direction for Data Engineering. Bring strong opinions grounded in experience while encouraging first-principles thinking. Guide architectural decisions and ensure the team builds systems that are simple, scalable, reliable, and appropriate for the problems we're solving.
Partner across the company. Work closely with Infrastructure, Analytics, Data Science, Product, Engineering, Finance, and other teams to understand how the business works, define clear ownership, and build a data ecosystem that enables teams to move faster and make better decisions.
Shape the future of the Data organization. Partner with the Head of Data on organizational design, hiring, roadmap prioritization, and the investments needed to support Imprint's continued growth.

Our Data Engineering priorities include:

Make Imprint's data legible. Lead the evolution of our enterprise data warehouse into a clear, consistent, and trusted representation of how Imprint's business works. Ensure important business concepts have well-designed models, clear definitions, and intuitive relationships that make our data easier to understand and use.
Raise the bar for analytics engineering. Establish strong principles and patterns for data modeling, transformation, testing, documentation, and ownership across our dbt and Snowflake environment. Create the technical standards that allow our data models to remain coherent as the business grows more complex.
Scale analytics engineering beyond the Data Engineering team. Create a development model where domain experts can turn their knowledge into high-quality, reusable data models without Data Engineering sitting in the critical path. Define the right boundaries, abstractions, review processes, and ownership model to make distributed contribution successful.
Build the platform that makes this possible. Partner closely with Infrastructure to create the tooling, workflows, and guardrails that make contributing to our enterprise data warehouse fast and safe. Make the right way the easiest way.

What We Look For

Experience introducing AI-assisted workflows at scale.
Experience in a high-growth startup, fintech, or another environment where data correctness and reliability are critical.
A track record of building and leading high-performing data or analytics engineering teams, including hiring exceptional talent, developing engineers, managing performance, and growing senior technical leaders.
Deep expertise in analytics engineering with dbt, with experience turning complex business domains into data models that are understandable, reusable, and trusted.
Strong technical judgment. You can evaluate data models and architecture, identify unnecessary complexity, challenge your team's thinking, and provide direction without needing to personally implement every solution.
Strong SQL fluency and enough familiarity with Python and modern software engineering practices to engage deeply with the team's technical work.
The ability to move comfortably between strategy and detail, pairing strong opinions with intellectual curiosity and first-principles thinking.

Perks & Benefits

Competitive compensation and equity packages
Leading configured work computers of your choice
Flexible paid time off
Fully covered, high-quality healthcare, including fully covered dependent coverage
Additional health coverage includes access to One Medical and the option to enroll in an FSA
20 weeks of paid parental leave for the primary caregiver and 8 weeks for all new parents
Access to industry-leading technology across all of our business units, stemming from our philosophy that we should invest in resources for our team that foster innovation, optimization, and productivity

Imprint welcomes talented individuals from all backgrounds who want to build the future of payments and rewards. If you are passionate about FinTech and eager to grow, let’s move the world forward, together.

In partnership with Finance, Product, and Engineering, mature and refine our FinOps practice to ensure infrastructure costs are optimized and aligned with customer value across public cloud, private cloud, and on-premises environments.

Demonstrated experience successfully driving platform maturity through consolidation, modernization, migration, standardization, and infrastructure optimization initiatives.

Experience leading and growing teams that build and manage infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tools such as Ansible, Terraform, CDK, CloudFormation, or equivalent automation frameworks.
Experience with observability and monitoring platforms such as Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, and related operational tooling.

Detail-oriented, organized, self-sufficient, and capable of finding creative solutions across business, product, platform, and organizational challenges.

jobs.description:
OUR COMPANY

SimX is a fast-growing company that has brought virtual and augmented reality to medical simulation training. At the end of 2024, we were acquired by Madison Industries, a partnership that has provided a surge in resources to accelerate our growth and mission. Our professional-grade VR system is the first of its kind, used by physicians, nurses, and paramedics to reduce medical errors and save lives.

Over the last decade, demand for our product has exploded; we are now used by 10 of the nation’s top 15 hospitals, including world-renowned institutions like the Cleveland Clinic, Mayo Clinic, and the University of Pennsylvania, our product is used around the world, and our technology is deployed across more than 50 US Military installations. We are looking for a mission-driven engineering leader to help us continue this momentum and achieve our mission to save lives around the world through better, faster, and more accessible simulation training.

THE MISSION

Reporting directly to the CEO, the Vice President of Engineering will be the executive leader of our engineering organization. Your mission is to further develop the maturity of our engineering organization, foster a culture of engineering excellence in a time of unprecedented change to engineering practices, and accelerate the delivery of our life-saving VR products. You will guide the evolution of our technical platform, ensuring it is robust, scalable, extensible, and capable of supporting our rapid growth as we scale toward $50M+ in ARR and beyond.

CORE RESPONSIBILITIES

Strategic Engineering Leadership & Vision
Partner with the CEO, CTO, and executive team to define and execute the technical and engineering roadmap, ensuring alignment with our mission, product strategy, and market expansion goals.
Architect a long-term engineering strategy that balances rapid feature delivery with scalable, secure, and maintainable infrastructure.
Define, track, and report engineering KPIs that give the executive team and Madison Industries leadership clear visibility into delivery, quality, and team health.
Adapt the engineering organization to the rapidly advancing frontier of engineering processes, including the ubiquitous use of AI tooling, in order to maximize the performance of the team.

Team Building & Organizational Scaling
Recruit, mentor, and develop a world-class, distributed engineering team, scaling the organization to support a business 10x its current size.
Establish robust engineering management practices, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous learning, and cross-functional collaboration.
Manage the company’s Engineering division, including direct reports at the Director level and technical leads and individual contributors through the reporting chain, and own its organizational design.
Develop a strong engineering leadership bench (managers and technical leads) and ensure they are capable of independently owning major engineering areas as the organization grows.

Engineering Execution and Effectiveness
Own the end-to-end software development lifecycle, driving disciplined agile practices that deliver predictable, high-quality releases.
Collaborate closely with Product, Operations, and Clinical Education teams to ensure engineering outputs consistently meet the rigorous standards required for professional healthcare training.
Drive operational excellence by ensuring adoption and continuous improvement of best practices (e.g., optimizing CI/CD pipelines, automating testing, reducing technical debt), as well as integrating new approaches (e.g., AI-driven testing, automated code reviews, etc.) when appropriate.

Architecture, Quality, & Security
Oversee the design and evolution of our platform architecture, ensuring high availability, performance, and scalability across global education, hospital and military deployments.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Enterprise Foundations
jobs.description:
We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Overview

Enterprise Foundations is the engineering team responsible for the architectural and integration work that allows Instacart's Retailer Platform to scale across the world's largest grocers. Our work spans omnichannel integrations — bringing products like FoodStorm catering and Caper Carts onto unified Instacart platform rails — enterprise extensibility (sandbox environments, configuration systems, retailer-facing tooling), and the cross-cutting data isolation work that allows Instacart's ML and Data Engineering teams to safely build per-retailer models on top of the platform. As Instacart's enterprise retail business expands to hundreds of partner brands and new international markets, this team's work is foundational to how the platform matures.

We are seeking a Senior Engineering Manager to lead this team of ~12 engineers. You'll set the unifying technical thesis for the team — multi-tenancy, data isolation, configuration-driven release management, and per-retailer extensibility — and drive the consolidation work that replaces bespoke per-vertical services with shared platform rails. In close partnership with Connected Stores, Pro Services, Commerce, Data Engineering, and ML, you'll broker the architectural and prioritization trade-offs that determine how Instacart serves enterprise retailers across multiple commerce surfaces.

About The Job

Lead, coach, and grow a senior-skewed team of ~12 engineers across multiple workstreams; set clear architectural and execution direction, develop talent, and foster a culture of ownership, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Set and maintain the unifying technical thesis for the team — multi-tenancy, data isolation, configuration-driven release management, and per-retailer extensibility — ensuring related workstreams converge on shared solutions rather than parallel implementations.
Drive consolidation of bespoke retailer-vertical services — catering order management, smart-cart backend logic, kiosk integrations, in-store mobile — onto unified Instacart platform rails, so each surface inherits Instacart's ranking, search, recommendations, and fulfillment.
Partner with ML and Data Engineering on long-term enterprise data platform compliance for our ML systems, ensuring per-retailer model training has the data, signals, and isolation it needs.
Deliver self-service tooling — including sandbox environments, configuration interfaces, and retailer-facing extensibility — that lets retailers and internal teams ship without engineering bottlenecks.
Represent technical and product trade-offs across multiple engineering and product organizations whose roadmaps and integration commitments evolve in real time; broker resourcing decisions, drive clarity in ambiguous scope, and ensure engineering investment stays aligned with committed work.

About You

Minimum Qualifications

8+ years of software engineering experience, including 3+ years managing engineering teams delivering platform or infrastructure products in a B2B or enterprise context.
Experience leading teams of 10+ engineers, including hiring, performance management, and career development of senior individual contributors.
Demonstrated success operating in ambiguous, high-growth environments where partner roadmaps, product coverage, and integration commitments are still maturing — with a track record of driving clarity and forward motion through that ambiguity.
Proven cross-functional leadership influencing outcomes across multiple engineering and product organizations, including comfort using structured escalation to unblock multi-team initiatives.
Experience leading multi-team architectural transitions such as consolidation, replatforming, multi-tenancy, or data isolation inside an established business with real customers and revenue.
Technical proficiency in distributed systems, API/SDK design, and cloud infrastructure (e.g., AWS or GCP).
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Preferred Qualifications

Direct domain experience in commerce platforms, omnichannel retail, OMS, POS, catering systems, or connected-store / in-store technology.
Track record of building multi-tenant platforms serving multiple internal or external customers, with per-tenant configuration, isolation, and extensibility requirements.
Experience partnering with ML and Data Engineering teams on data platform compliance, model training infrastructure, or data isolation initiatives.
Background scaling enterprise integrations and managing partner-facing technical relationships across product, engineering, and customer-facing functions.
Experience leading other engineering managers and growing two-layer organizations.

Instacart provides highly market-competitive compensation and benefits in each location where our employees work. This role is remote and the base pay range for a successful candidate is dependent on their permanent work location. Please review our Flex First remote work policy here.

Offers may vary based on many factors, such as candidate experience and skills required for the role. Additionally, this role is eligible for a new hire equity grant as well as annual refresh grants. Please read more about our benefits offerings here.

jobs.description:
This is an exciting opportunity to direct the Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) engineering team within Natera's Data Science Production Engineering (DSPE) organization. In this leadership role, you will oversee the ExHS team's entire operation, ensuring the team's timely and accurate data analytics support to production teams, e.g., product management team, lab operations teams, lab director teams, and genetic counselor teams, within a CLIA/FDA regulated environment.

Important Note:
This Director needs to be available during the extended hours (e.g., early morning, late evening, and weekend hours) during emergencies or other critical events. The Director does not require general availability during the extended hours, but only during emergencies or other critical events during the extended hours.

Primary Responsibilities

Team Leadership and Operations

Direct and mentor a team of 10+ ExHS data science support engineers and analysts providing coverage across standard and extended operational shifts, for the timely and accurate data analytics support for production teams.
Enforce operating procedures for compliance, quality, and efficiency.
Measure, report, and continuously improve team operational effectiveness.
Lead the team during critical production incidents or emergency events during and outside standard business hours.

Technical Execution and Infrastructure

Develop and maintain technologies for operational visibility (e.g., via AWS QuickSight or Streamlit).
Develop and maintain technologies for operational efficiency.
Manage and execute analytics workflows on Snowflake and AWS infrastructure (Redshift, Athena, Batch, EC2, S3), and ensure strictly compliance to CLIA, FDA, and internal quality management standards.

Process Improvement

Improve operating procedures for compliance, quality, and efficiency.
Train and coach team members on new technologies, procedures, and guidelines/best practices.
Identify areas for improvement within the DSPE ExHS team, develop improvement solutions, and/or work with DSPE teams to implement such solutions.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

Represent the Extended-Hours Support (ExHS) teams in stakeholder meetings.
Proactively manage stakeholder expectations.
Establish regular stakeholder reporting mechanisms.
Translate complex analytical results into actionable recommendations for cross-functional partners.

Qualifications

Master's degree in Statistics, Data Science, Bioinformatics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or Operations Research required; Doctorate degrees are a plus.
Minimum 8 years of relevant industry experience with a Master's degree (or minimum 4 years with a Doctorate).
Minimum 3 years of experience operating within a highly regulated environment (CLIA and/or FDA compliant settings).
Minimum 3 years of management experience leading medium-sized teams (e.g., of 7 to 20 engineers or analysts, or larger) in production support or operational roles.
Working knowledge of diagnostic laboratory business processes and genomic/bioinformatics technologies.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

Proficient in data analysis and statistical techniques.
Proficient in Python and SQL development.
Hands-on experience with Snowflake platform technologies and AWS cloud analytics tooling (Redshift, Athena, Batch, EC2, S3).
Demonstrated experience developing operational dashboards and analytical tools using AWS QuickSight, Streamlit, or equivalent platforms.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of building cross-functional trust and explaining technical data clearly.
Ability to navigate operational ambiguity, establish structure where gaps exist, and resolve production bottlenecks directly.
Good documentation practices and coding style.
Strong integrity.
Team player, collaborative.

Compensation & Total Rewards

This range reflects a good-faith estimate of the base pay we reasonably expect to offer at the time of hire. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations.

This position is also eligible for additional compensation and benefits through Natera’s robust Total Rewards program, including:

Annual performance incentive bonus
Long-term equity awards
Comprehensive health benefits (medical, dental, vision)
401(k) with company match
Generous paid time off and company holidays
Additional wellness and work-life benefits

OUR OPPORTUNITY

Natera™ is a global leader in cell-free DNA (cfDNA) testing, dedicated to oncology, women’s health, and organ health. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives.

The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. Meet with various public or private entities or individuals to discuss issues relating to a variety of engineering/construction challenges and programs.
Ensure technical reports and presentations explain research, findings, and recommendations to prevent, control, restore, or address design, and/or construction issues or opportunities.
Have or demonstrably can develop a client base for providing high level geotechnical/geological engineering services including identifying additional business development opportunities.
Mentor staff to support their growth and professional development.

jobs.description:
About Viam

Founded by Eliot Horowitz, co-founder and former CTO of MongoDB, Viam is a novel robotics engineering platform that lets you configure, control, and manage robots intuitively and quickly. We're inspiring a generation of engineers to solve complicated automation problems with our uniquely powerful suite of software tools.

We're a ~100-person company headquartered in New York City.

Senior Product Manager, Platform

About the Role

Hybrid 3 days/week in NYC office

We're looking for a Senior Product Manager to own a core area of the Viam platform. You'll set the roadmap for your area, define how product and engineering make decisions together, and partner with senior leadership on strategy: what keeps developers from adopting Viam, which experiences become bottlenecks, and where physical AI and robotics are heading with respect to how software engineers get involved.

You have worked as a software engineer, which is a hard requirement here; the role sits close enough to the code that it does not work otherwise. Prior robotics or IoT experience isn't required, but you should be excited to work close to hardware and physical systems.

What you'll do:

Own the roadmap for your area of the platform, from problem definition through launch and adoption, and decide what ships, what waits, and what gets deprecated.
Collaborate on product strategy: what keeps developers from adopting Viam, and which experiences become bottlenecks or blockers.
Develop a view on where physical AI and robotics are heading, and what that means for how software engineers get involved.
Work with engineering leads on the decisions that shape platform architecture, like what belongs in the core, in the registry, or in an SDK.
Take new capabilities from 0 to 1 and stay on them through real customer deployments.
Own the developer experience for your area, including SDK ergonomics, API surface, docs, and onboarding.
Define success against developer adoption and second activations, and use that to decide what to build next and what to cut.
Bring what you learn from customers and Forward Deployed engineers back into the roadmap, and build the product practice itself as you go.

What you bring:

Experience as a software engineer, building and shipping production software used by real users, plus 8+ years in product management since. The engineering background is a requirement, not a preference.
Experience building developer-facing or infrastructure products like APIs, SDKs, or platforms, where the user is an engineer.
A track record of taking products from ambiguity to production, including migrations, deprecations, and breaking changes that real customers depend on.
Technical credibility with engineers. You can run the SDK yourself, read the code well enough to ask the right question, and hold your own in a design review.
Ability to do real market research and form a product strategy from it, rather than execute one handed to you. This includes time spent directly with users in their own environment.
Comfort defining success metrics and using data to decide what to build next.
Ability to move quickly, decide with incomplete information, wear whatever hat the week requires, and change direction when the evidence changes.
Experience working with senior leadership, including setting direction and disagreeing well.
Hands-on interest in hardware, IoT, embedded systems, or similar physical systems. Professional robotics experience is not required.

The salary for this role is between $180K - $240K /year.

Vision Driven
Collaborate Openly
Act Decisively
Succeed Through Diversity
Hold Ourselves Accountable
Lead with Curiosity

jobs.title: Vice President, Platform
jobs.description:
Vice President, Platform — Intelligence & Leverage

Glendale, CA — on-site, 5 days a week

Full-time
Compensation:
$175,000-$250,000

About Bambee
Bambee started as a subscription service delivering HR support to small businesses across the United States, and grew into a leading provider of direct HR guidance for small and midsized companies.
For the last two years we have concentrated nearly all of our R&D capacity — and a disproportionate amount of founder and executive attention — on Bionic, our proprietary AI architecture. That work defined a new category: Cloud Workforce Operations
, the continuous management of the systems that determine how a workforce operates, including its people, policies, performance, communication, compliance, and organizational health.
Hexagon is the platform at the center of it. Instead of waiting for a company to ask for help, Hexagon observes what is happening, understands what should be true, identifies the gaps, decides what happens next, and coordinates or executes the work to close them. Every completed operation makes the system more capable.

About the Role
Every major product and operating decision Bambee makes over the next five years will be made cheaper, faster, or more expensive by architectural choices made in the next twelve months. We are looking for the person who owns those choices.
The Vice President, Platform owns Bambee's Intelligence & Leverage System: the shared technical and intelligence architecture through which data, models, reasoning, memory, agents, orchestration, and reusable platform capabilities make every Bambee product and internal operating system more capable.
You own what Bambee's systems can know, reason about, remember, execute, and reuse. You decide what gets built once and inherited everywhere, where system boundaries belong, what must stay stable, what should be deprecated, and where temporary speed creates unacceptable long-term cost.
Our operating principle is Outcome → Intelligence → System → Human Judgment → Headcount.
The sequence is intentional, and you are one of its primary architects.
You will be judged by whether every new product, agent, workflow, and operating system inherits more capability than the one before it.

What You Will Own
1. Intelligence architecture.
The architecture connecting organizational data, persistent context, models, reasoning, memory, evaluation, learning, and execution. You will define how the system holds company context, retrieves memory, invokes models, evaluates outputs, and improves its next decision. The objective is not more models — it is one coherent intelligence system that products inherit instead of rebuilding.
2. Primitives, reuse, and compounding.
Which capabilities get built once and inherited everywhere: identity, permissions, organizational state, memory, orchestration, agents, execution, evaluation, auditability, documents, integrations. You also own the tooling, testing, evaluation, and deployment architecture that lets teams move independently without recreating foundational work. The measure is whether the next capability is easier to build than the last one, because the platform already contains more of what it needs.
3. Autonomy and orchestration.
Hexagon already observes, assesses, diagnoses, recommends, coordinates, and performs selected categories of work on its own. That scope will widen. You will architect how agents are orchestrated, how work routes between machines and humans, how confidence and risk determine autonomy, how exceptions are handled, and how outcomes are verified — more operational capability, with real control and observability.
4. Data, extensibility, reliability, and security.
The core data model, system-of-record architecture, APIs, integrations, versioning, multi-tenant boundaries, reliability, security, access control, observability, infrastructure cost, and backward compatibility. You will define how organizations, employees, policies, assessments, recommendations, actions, and outcomes are represented, and build the integration surface connecting Hexagon to the systems customers already use. Reliability, security, and infrastructure economics are architectural inputs, not downstream concerns.
5. Organizational leverage.
The platform should make Bambee itself more capable, not only its products. You will work across Finance, Product, Growth, Operations, Customer, and Frontier to find repeated cognition, fragmented information, duplicated logic, and manual coordination that should become shared system capability. When several teams solve the same problem, ask whether the platform should solve it once. When people are acting as middleware between systems, ask whether that coordination can be encoded. When a function needs linear headcount to handle rising complexity, ask whether the platform can change the economics of the work.

The Backgrounds We Find Most Interesting
We are not optimizing for a conventional platform-management résumé. The strongest candidate may have been a CTO, Chief Architect, Head of AI Platform, VP Engineering, or a technical founder:
Technical founder or former CTO
who built foundational architecture, then had to connect technical decisions to products, customers, and economics
AI or ML platform architect
who moved past isolated modeling into production systems involving context, retrieval, reasoning, agents, orchestration, and evaluation
Data or platform leader
who grew from shared services into systems that make data actionable through models, reasoning, and automation
Distributed-systems architect
with strong product judgment
Technical product or platform leader
who owned shared architecture while staying close to what the business needed it to enable

We care more about the systems you have personally shaped than the progression of your titles.

What We Look For
Architecture depth.
You reason deeply about data, distributed systems, APIs, AI systems, reliability, security, and cost. You can descend into the architecture rather than managing it from abstraction, and you know when an attractive abstraction is masking a weak boundary. You have made consequential architecture decisions and built judgment from the ones that worked and the ones that did not.
Intelligence-systems thinking.
You understand that AI infrastructure is larger than models, and can reason about how context, memory, retrieval, agents, orchestration, evaluation, and feedback loops form a single coherent system. You can tell product-specific intelligence from shared infrastructure, and you know the quality of an intelligent system depends on what it knows, remembers, and verifies — not only on what it can generate.
Leverage instinct.
You would rather delete two redundant systems than build a third one to coordinate them. You get suspicious when several teams solve the same problem independently. You think about architecture in economic terms: marginal cost, coordination cost, reuse, compounding capability. You will say no when short-term speed creates structural cost, and you will not use architecture as an excuse for delay.

Why Bambee
We take on some of the hardest problems in workforce operations because solving them unlocks disproportionately ambitious outcomes. We are building it for ordinary companies and the people who spend their lives inside them.
If that sounds like the kind of company — and the kind of system — you want to help build, we should talk.

jobs.title: Enterprise Engineering Systems Director
jobs.description:
The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space.

Building on The Aerospace Corporation's reputation as a trusted, impartial advisor with integrity and dedication to mission success, the Civil Systems Group (CSG) combines deep technical expertise with market-leading innovation to help our customers solve complex systems engineering and integration challenges. CSG is organized by core customer-facing lines of business to manage and grow programs within NASA, NOAA, and the NNSA, while extending our capabilities to other civilian federal government agencies fully integrated within Aerospace rules, regulations, processes, values, and behaviors.

We are looking for an Enterprise Engineering Systems Director
(Systems Director – Systems and Digital Engineering)
. As a Systems Director in the Civil Systems Group within Defense, you will provide leadership, planning and direction to an experienced team of engineers and work closely with Engineering Technical Managers to support the mission area of the Department of Energy (DOE) National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) Office of Defense Programs (DP). You will lead and manage your team to accomplish systems engineering/analysis to various Defense Program tasks in support of our Nation. You will mentor your team to leverage Aerospace’s vast network of subject matter experts to bring innovative solutions to NNSA’s hardest problems. Additionally, you will look to identify new opportunities/challenges to leverage Aerospace capabilities to apply to our NNSA customer.

This is a full-time position based in Albuquerque, NM, Crystal City, VA, Colorado Springs, CO, or El Segundo, CA which requires a minimum of 4 days/week onsite work.

What You’ll Be Doing

Work closely with Principal Director and the rest of the management team to lead and manage Aerospace Enterprise Engineering team members with the challenging issues Aerospace is tackling for Defense Programs within the National Nuclear Security Administration.
Supports establishment of the Enterprise Engineering organization's objectives/goals with Principal Director and communicate them to your subordinates and interfacing organizations.
Provide strategic leadership and conducts activities consistent with corporate policies/practices, goals, and objectives.
Participates with higher management in determining the organization's structure and staff including resource needs (budget planning and allocation of resources).
Reports the organization's activities, progress, and achievements through written and oral reports to management, subordinates, and customers.
Coordinates work activities within the organization; monitors workload, work progress, and schedules; ensures completion of organization's work assignments within cost and schedule guidelines.
Seeks and identifies opportunities for additional, expanded, and new business and assists Sr. management in evaluating and pursuing new possibilities.
Cooperates and communicates frequently with customers to coordinate and report work progress, issues, and results.
Conducts staff performance reviews and recommends performance improvement, career development, salary, and promotion actions; establishes staffing needs; advises reassignments, training, transfers, and other staff deployments; and assists other supervisors in evaluating and assigning staff.
Directs technical group performing engineering design, analysis, or other research and development activities.
Lead from the front to influence customers to field more integrated solutions.

What You Need to be Successful - Systems Director – Systems Engineering and Digital Engineering

Minimum Requirements

Bachelor's degree in engineering, science, or another appropriate technical discipline
12 or more years of progressively responsible professional engineering/scientific experience
Experience in a managerial/leadership role with proven ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with all levels of contractors, customers, and corporate staff
Demonstrated networking, teaming, management, and leadership skills within a program office or matrixed technical organization, building and leading project teams, formulating task plans, ensuring product quality, and effectively interacting with customers.
Proven technical credibility across a broad set of systems engineering topics, and a deep understanding of the engineering of complex systems
Experience working with U.S. government agencies such as DOE/NNSA and DoD
Demonstrated strong interpersonal, organizational, written, and oral communication skills
Availability to travel domestically, up to 25% of the time
This position requires a current and active Top Secret or Q security clearance, which is issued by the U.S. government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance.

How You Can Stand Out

It would be impressive if you have one or more of these:

Advanced degree in engineering or math with specific experience in Systems/Digital Engineering
Familiarity with the DOE and NNSA National Laboratories in the Defense Programs Arena
Knowledge of the Aerospace Engineering and Technology Group (ETG) skills and capabilities
Demonstrated ability to create solutions to address national security needs
Holds a TS or DOE Q clearance with ability to obtain SCI

We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. The grade-based pay range for this job is listed below. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills.

(Min - Max)

$168,200.00 - $252,400.00

Pay Basis: Annual

Leadership Competencies

Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who:

Operate Strategically
Lead Change  
Engage with Impact  
Foster Innovation  
Deliver Results

Ways We Reward Our Employees

During your interview process, our team will provide details of our industry-leading benefits.

Benefits vary and are applicable based on Job Type. A few highlights include:

Comprehensive health care and wellness plans
Paid holidays, sick time, and vacation
Standard and alternate work schedules, including telework options
401(k) Plan — Employees receive a total company-paid benefit of 8%, 10%, or 12% of eligible compensation based on years of service and matching contributions; employees are immediately eligible and vested in the plan upon hire
Flexible spending accounts
Variable pay program for exceptional contributions
Relocation assistance
Professional growth and development programs to help advance your career
Education assistance programs
An inclusive work environment built on teamwork, flexibility, and respect

We are all unique, from various backgrounds and all walks of life, yet one thing bonds all of us to each other—the belief that we can make a difference. This core belief empowers us to do our best work at The Aerospace Corporation.

Equal Opportunity Commitment
