jobs.title: Director of Software Development
jobs.description:
About Karmak

Karmak is a 100% employee-owned software company that has helped keep the commercial transportation industry moving for more than 40 years. Our flagship platform, Karmak Fusion
, powers the parts, service, accounting, and business operations of heavy-duty truck dealerships and transportation companies across North America. Simply put, our customers keep America moving-and we build the technology that helps them do it.

We develop on the Microsoft technology stack, including .NET, SQL Server, and Microsoft Azure
, creating modern, scalable solutions for a mission-critical industry. As employee-owners, we think beyond our individual roles and share responsibility for our company's success. We're looking for leaders who embrace that same ownership mindset and are excited to make a lasting impact.

Position Summary

Remote (US); limited travel (1–2 trips per year)

The Director of Software Development is responsible for the management and daily execution of Karmak's development organization in support of Karmak Fusion. Leading through four development managers spanning application development, QA, and database/reporting teams (a 30+ person engineering organization), this position owns the flow of work between Support, Implementation, Product, DBA, and the development teams; serves as the development-side approval authority on customer patches; and makes go/no-go decisions across a multi-version release train.

The Director is the primary point of escalation into development for the rest of the organization and the VP of Development's operational right hand - a role requiring the technical credibility to challenge a root-cause analysis, the judgment to weigh customer risk on every patch and release decision, and the leadership to run cross-team incident response when a customer-impacting issue crosses team boundaries.

How You'll Operate

This role is built for a high-agency leader. Here is the working relationship you should expect:

You'll get context and priorities from the VP of Development - not task lists. We expect you to identify what will move the needle, commit to outcomes, and run with them. You bring the VP problems with proposed answers, not open questions.
This is not a hands-on coding role, but you haven't stopped being an engineer. You can read C# and SQL, sit in architecture and root-cause reviews and challenge them, and tell a real fix from a symptom patch. Senior engineers respect you because of it.
You own escalations end to end: you move them, you don't track them. When plans change, you re-plan in hours, not weeks, and keep the train moving.
You communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided. Exceptions come with verified data, options, and a recommendation.

What You'll Own In Year One

Success in this role is measured in outcomes, not activity. In your first year, a home run looks like:

Release predictability - Releases and patches across the multi-version release train ship on schedule with fewer defect escapes, and go/no-go discipline holds at every checkpoint - without the VP in the room.
Escalations owned and closed - Escalations from Support, Implementation, and Product get a single accountable owner, are driven to root cause rather than symptom fixes, and are closed with clear communication - they stop bouncing upward.
AI-assisted development adoption - The organization measurably advances on AI-assisted engineering - code analysis, automated review, test automation, and agentic tooling - with honest evaluation of where it multiplies velocity and where it doesn't.
Manager bench strength - The four development managers grow into leaders who plan, prioritize, and make sound calls with less direction - the organization runs well when you step away from it.

Essential Job Functions

Provide technical leadership and direction to the development managers and their teams, assisting with planning, prioritization, technology assessment, professional development, and cross-team coordination
Serve as the development-side approval authority on customer patches, weighing patch-versus-upgrade paths, deployment risk windows, and multi-version complexity; ensure patch decisions protect both the customer and the maintainability of the release line
Own go/no-go decisions at each release checkpoint - integration close, QA greenlight, smoke test, packaging, and staged customer rollout - including the authority to hold or pause a release when quality or customer risk demands it
Serve as the primary point of escalation to development for Support, Implementation, and Product; route issues to the correct team or subject-matter expert, chase them to closure, and keep requestors informed with clear status and next steps
Lead incident response for customer-impacting issues that cross team boundaries; drive to root cause rather than symptom fixes, convene the right people quickly, and communicate resolution paths to stakeholders
Direct the daily product delivery rhythm in partnership with Support, DBA, Installations, and Product, and chair recurring quality reviews with the support organization, converting findings into tracked work items
Keep the VP of Development ahead of surprises: escalate exceptions with verified data, options, and a recommendation; draft customer-facing technical communications for executive review
Manage relationships with external technical consultants and vendors in support of development initiatives
Champion continuous improvement of engineering practice, including branch and merge policy, automated code review, test automation, and AI-assisted development tooling
Manage the personnel activities of the team to include hiring, training, and evaluating employees; lead merit and salary planning through the development managers
Lead the team in change management and effectively apply new process improvements
Embrace self-development, professional growth, and desire for feedback for individual growth
Maintain confidentiality
Be a champion for Karmak and the team

Essential Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Bachelor's degree (B.A./B.S.) in Computer Science or a related field and a minimum of 10 years of software development experience, including 5+ years leading developers and experience managing managers or an organization of 30+ engineers; or equivalent combination of education and experience
Required: current technical depth on the Microsoft development stack - able to read and reason about .NET code (C#/VB.NET) and Microsoft SQL Server (T-SQL, database design, query performance) well enough to be credible with senior engineers, interrogate a root-cause analysis, and distinguish a real fix from a symptom patch
Strongly preferred: experience running teams that build and operate on Microsoft Azure (PaaS services, cloud architecture) and Azure DevOps for work tracking, pipelines, and release management
Direct experience owning production release and patch decisions for commercial, customer-installed or hosted software, including versioned release trains and customer-impact risk assessment; ERP or other business-critical domain experience strongly preferred
A demonstrated pattern of high-agency ownership: identifying what matters, driving it to done without waiting for direction, and being accountable for outcomes, not just process
Demonstrated pattern of calm incident leadership and cross-functional coordination across support, QA, DBA, and product organizations
Exceptional team leadership skills, including the ability to effectively coach, motivate, and empower team members and develop the judgment of front-line managers
Ability to build and sustain trusted relationships internally and externally, sound judgment in dealing with business issues, and the instinct to communicate proactively upward so leadership is never blindsided
Strong initiative, teamwork, and interpersonal skills; strong written and verbal communication skills, including drafting customer-facing technical communications
Capable of working in a growth-oriented environment, with ability to manage and prioritize multiple concurrent requests, projects, and responsibilities
Hands-on experience adopting AI-assisted development practices (code analysis, automated review, agentic tooling) preferred
Knowledge of the heavy-duty or commercial transportation industry a plus

The above statements describe the general nature and level of work being performed in this job. They are not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties. Additional responsibilities may be assigned by Karmak.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Energy Storage
jobs.description:
SOLV Energy is a leading provider of infrastructure services to the power industry, designing, building and maintaining utility scale solar, battery storage and high voltage substation projects nationwide.

Job Description Summary:

The Director of Engineering, Energy Storage leads, mentors, and develops SOLV Energy’s Energy Storage Engineering team. Oversees the design of energy storage systems for utility-scale renewable energy projects, ensuring compliance with technical standards, safety regulations, and project requirements. Drives innovation, implements value engineering strategies, and maintains quality and reliability across all energy storage deliverables.

This role can be fully remote or hybrid, with regular in-office presence in San Diego, CA. Up to 50% travel is required. Specific location details and expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

Job Description:

This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned

Position Responsibilities and Duties:

Department Management/Leadership

Hire, manage, and mentor a diverse team of engineers, focused on energy storage systems and design.
Foster effective communication and collaboration between the Energy Storage Engineering group and cross-functional teams, including internal and external engineers, business development managers, project managers, pre-construction managers, procurement specialists, schedulers, estimators, and construction teams.
Allocate resources effectively to meet project deadlines and ensure optimal team utilization.
Overall management and responsibility of SOLV Energy Storage Engineering team, including establishing and maintaining department goals, budgets, and performance metrics.
Establish and maintain partnerships with a diverse group of third-party Engineers-of-Record (EORs).
Represent SOLV Engineering and management in customer and client meetings.

Technical Oversight

Oversee development of Energy Storage engineering standards and procurement specifications.
Implement and maintain quality control processes to ensure designs comply with all owner, SOLV, AHJ, and vendor requirements.
Proactively identify and resolve potential design and construction challenges and coordinate with various stakeholders to develop cost-effective solutions.
Lead design efforts for interconnection systems, including coordinating utility approvals, ISO and NERC compliance, and energization plans.

Strategic Initiatives

Drive adoption of new technologies and best practices to optimize system performance, reliability, and cost.
Develop innovative, customer-centric engineering solutions that address client needs, reduce cost, and enhance project value.
Represent SOLV Energy team as a technical subject matter expert (SME) during client interviews/meetings as required.
Stay informed on industry best practices and technological advancements in utility-scale energy storage design.
Stay informed on relevant regulations, codes, and guidelines that may impact future SOLV project designs.
Provide SME guidance/consultation to other departments within SOLV, as needed.
Training and Development
Identify training and development needs and provide opportunities for skills enhancement and professional growth.
Develop and mentor staff for career advancement.

Minimum Skills or Experience Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering (preferred).
10+ years of experience in engineering with a focus on Energy Storage, renewables, or power systems in an EPC or Owner/Engineer environment.
Minimum 5+ years of experience in management
Professional Engineer (PE) license is preferred.
Ability to travel up to 50% of the time will be needed.
Proven track record of successfully designing and delivering utility-scale Energy Storage projects.

jobs.title: Director of Software
jobs.description:
Join a fast growing startup in a role that blends cutting edge biotech with the cutting edge software.

This is a full time, in-person role at our office in Marina del Rey, CA.

About the Company:

Mango is building a new type of microscope. Our innovative approach enables us to grow microbes and observe their growth in real time. Mango is through the PoC phase with several top 10 biopharma companies and currently launching a GMP product. You would be joining at a critical juncture in the business.

Located in Los Angeles, our team combines expertise in business, mechanical engineering, bioengineering, and software development. We've honed our skills at various startups, including Snapchat, and now we're focused on turning this groundbreaking idea into a practical tool for pharmaceutical manufacturing. We're eager to find someone who shares our enthusiasm for making a meaningful impact.

The software at Mango truly spans the full stack from the firmware running on the instrument, a custom imaging stack,  image process and machine learning on a petabyte-scale internal set of novel biological data, and a well-designed performant UI/UX for our customers.

Position Summary:

We are seeking a Director of Software to lead Mango into the next stage of growth for both the company and the software team. We expect strong hands-on technical skills in addition to technical leadership experience. The Director of Software acts as principal architect, business liaison for software, project manager and trusted ear to leadership. They are responsible for all things software, both the delivery of the customer facing software and internal tools integral to training our state of the art ML models or organizing our massive data warehouse.

Key Responsibilities:

Leadership and Communication: Work directly with the rest of senior leadership to define business objectives, key milestones and product initiatives coalescing into a software roadmap. Maintain alignment cross-functionally and execute on the software roadmap. Continue to build a highly effective software team as the company enters a growth phase.
Design and Development: Act as principal architect for a complex full stack software product that involves generation, processing and display of terabytes of data per day at each deployment.
Collaboration: Work in close coordination with Mechanical, Electrical, and Biology teams to define the product and timelines. Perform cross-functional design review and make business critical decisions.
Quality and Compliance: Own the software compliance effort and handle customer relationships from the software perspective. Ensure a high standard of engineering across the software team. Meet regulatory requirements and anticipate customer compliance needs.

General Qualifications:

8-10 years of relevant industry experience.
Experience interfacing directly with C-suite in defining engineering goals for the business.
Strong understanding of high level tradeoffs with respect to product/business/engineering.
Demonstrated ability to face unique challenges with persistence, creativity, and a positive attitude.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, crucial for documentation and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Experience with the regulatory and compliance landscape of pharmaceutical and biotech companies

jobs.title: Director of Engineering
jobs.description:
About Allia Technology

Allia Health Group builds technology across multiple healthcare brands — Brello / HelloWellness, Southend Pharmacy, and Allia Care. Our Technology organisation runs on a deliberate operating model: an upstream Strategy & Execution engine that turns brand strategy into a ranked, capacity-feasible roadmap reflecting only committed value, and a downstream AI-Native Technology Operating System (AIN-TOS) that delivers it through a 4-quarter roadmap, two-week Linear cycles, capacity-mapped pods, and a shared operating system of standards (design, engineering, QA, agent OS, security, observability).

We are scaling the leadership of this organisation. As the CTO concentrates on Artificial Intelligence and Robotics, we are creating a Director of Engineering to own the build-and-run heart of the function: Software, Cloud & Security, and Internal IT.

The Role

The Director of Engineering is the single accountable owner for how Allia builds, ships, secures and runs its platforms and internal systems. You will lead three functions — Software, Cloud & Security, and Internal IT — covering roughly 19+ engineers and specialists across frontend, backend, fullstack, QA automation, cloud/DevOps, security (SecOps and GRC), and internal IT operations.

You own delivery and reliability end to end, operating the engineering functions against AIN-TOS so the CTO is free to focus on the frontier. You translate the committed roadmap into shipped, high-quality, secure software on a predictable rhythm — protecting capacity honesty, enforcing the shared OS, and keeping pods autonomous but coherent.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who has run multi-team engineering organisations, cares about operating discipline as much as technical excellence, and can hold reliability, security and delivery accountable simultaneously.

What You Will Own

Engineering delivery. Accountable for shipping the committed roadmap across Brello, Patient Platform, Realtime Data Hub, Zito Care and supporting platforms. Run fixed two-week Linear cycles as the single delivery rhythm; map team capacity against cycle priorities; close cycles with demos and retros that feed the learning loop.

Platform reliability and cloud. Own cloud architecture, infrastructure and DevOps (AWS / GCP). Accountable for uptime, performance, incident response and the operational health of everything in production.

Security posture. Own security strategy and execution across SecOps and GRC, including the path to and maintenance of SOC2. Ensure security validation is built into delivery controls before release, not bolted on after.

Internal IT. Own internal systems, identity and access management, user management, web operations and procurement — the systems the whole company depends on.

The shared OS. Maintain and evolve engineering standards, QA standards, deployment frameworks and observability as shared infrastructure that pods consume rather than rebuild. Local autonomy, global coherence.

Talent and structure. Lead, coach and grow three function heads and their teams. Close open positions (Software, Cloud & Security and Internal IT currently carry open seats), uplevel capability, and build a bench.

Translate, commit, report. In our decision-rights model, technology leadership translates strategy into demand, runs assessment and capacity mapping, and reports committed versus realised value. You carry that responsibility for the engineering functions and represent them in the executive operating cadence.

How You Will Work

You will operate inside an established, opinionated operating model. Success means running it well, not replacing it:

Capacity is honest. Capacity is real, not aspirational. You and your leads protect it. The roadmap reflects only what can actually be delivered.
Pods own delivery. Pods are autonomous, integrated, and free of a central queue. You set standards and remove blockers; you do not become the bottleneck.
Commitment is two-sided. Engineering commits to deliver; quality and security controls are non-negotiable gates before release.
Override is visible. Recommendations and overrides are separate and both logged. Decisions are transparent.
Learning compounds. Every release feeds the shared OS. Incidents, retros and adoption data become standards, prompts and infrastructure.

You will run the bi-weekly cycle cadence (planning, cycle-close demos, retros) and the weekly rhythm (intake triage, cycle health, blockers cleared), and contribute to the monthly portfolio review and quarterly roadmap rebuild.

What We Are Looking For
Must Have

8+ years in software engineering with 4+ years leading engineering organisations, including managing managers / function leads.
Proven track record shipping production software on a predictable delivery cadence across multiple teams.
Strong command of modern cloud infrastructure (AWS and/or GCP), DevOps practices, and production reliability at scale.
Real ownership of security in an engineering context — comfortable being accountable for security posture and compliance (SOC2 or equivalent).
Experience operating within a structured delivery system (cycles/sprints, capacity planning, defined standards) and the discipline to protect it.
A builder of people: hiring, coaching, levelling and retaining strong engineers.
Clear, executive-level communicator who can translate between strategy and delivery and report committed vs. realised value credibly.

Strongly Preferred

Experience across the full stack of functions you'll own — software delivery, cloud/infra, security, and internal IT — or a demonstrated ability to lead functions outside your original specialism.
Background in regulated or healthcare environments, or other settings where security, compliance and reliability are first-class.
Familiarity with AI-native engineering practices and agent-based tooling (we run an "agent OS" as part of our shared OS).
Experience with Linear (or comparable) as a system of record for delivery.

How You Lead

You treat operating discipline as a feature, not overhead.
You make capacity and commitments honest, even when the answer is uncomfortable.
You give teams autonomy and hold them to shared standards.
You are calm and decisive in incidents, and you make every incident a source of compounding improvement.

Why This Role Matters

This is one of the most consequential leadership hires in Allia Technology. You will take direct ownership of the engineering, platform, security and IT backbone of a multi-brand healthcare technology group — and in doing so, you free our most senior technologist to drive the AI and Robotics work that will define our advantage. You inherit a working operating model, a committed roadmap, and strong function leads. Your job is to make the build-and-run engine excellent, reliable and secure, and to lead it with the autonomy of a true owner.

jobs.title: Director of Software Engineering, Behaviors and Planning
jobs.description:
About Overland AI

Founded in 2022 and headquartered in Seattle, Washington, Overland AI is transforming land operations for modern defense. The company leverages over a decade of advanced research in robotics and machine learning, as well as a field-test forward ethos, to deliver combined capabilities for unit commanders. Our OverDrive autonomy stack enables ground vehicles to navigate and operate off-road in any terrain without GPS or direct operator control. Our intuitive OverWatch C2 interface provides commanders with precise coordination capabilities essential for mission success.

Overland AI has secured funding from prominent defense tech investors including 8VC and Point 72, and built trusted partnerships with DARPA, the U.S. Army, Marine Corps, and Special Operations Command. Backed by eight-figure contracts across the Department of Defense, we are strengthening national security by iterating closely with end users engaged in tactical operations.

About The Role

Overland AI builds autonomous ground vehicles for defense and national security missions. Our Behaviors & Planning team owns the final layer of single-vehicle autonomy: using terrain understanding to generated planned paths and execute behaviors. This is the core autonomy loop that makes our vehicles move safely and reliably across operational domains ranging from secondary roads to complex off-road terrain.

We are looking for a Director to lead this team. You will manage 7-10 engineers working across motion planning, on-vehicle behaviors, geospatial planning, and offline verification. You will set technical direction for how our vehicles navigate the world autonomously, partner closely with our ML & Perception team to drive tighter integration between learned terrain models and classical planning, and own the verification systems that prove our autonomy works before it reaches the field.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will shape the technical roadmap, make architecture decisions, mentor engineers, and represent your team's capabilities and needs across the organization. The work matters: soldiers depend on our vehicles to operate reliably in contested, communication-degraded, and GPS-denied environments.

What You'll Do

Lead the team.

Manage, mentor, and grow a team of 7-10 engineers spanning planning, behaviors, and verification. Run sprint planning and set technical priorities. Build a team culture that values engineering rigor and field-validated results.

Own the autonomy loop.

Drive the technical direction for single-vehicle autonomous movement: local and mid-range planning (MPPI, costmap-based approaches), global/geospatial planning, behavior management (teleop, autonomous modes, trail-keeping, convoy following), and task interfaces. Ensure the system is safe, performant, and reliable across our full operational design domain.

Close the loop with perception.

Your primary technical partnership is with our ML & Perception team. Perception provides terrain understanding products (ground surface prediction, costmap prediction, dynamic object prediction); your team consumes these to plan and execute. You will co-own the contract between these teams and drive tighter integration as we move toward end-to-end learned planning approaches.

Build the verification story.

Own offline verification of autonomy requirements through simulation, log playback, and automated regression testing. The team that writes behaviors also proves they work. You will invest in tooling and infrastructure that lets your team catch regressions before they reach vehicles.

Push the frontier.

Explore and integrate emerging capabilities such as VLM-based reasoning for behavioral guardrails, scene understanding, and contextual decision-making. This is the per-vehicle intelligence that enables effective multi-robot orchestration at the mission level.

Represent autonomy in the field.

Support field deployments and customer demonstrations. Understand soldier workflows and operational needs firsthand. Translate field observations into engineering priorities.

PhD in robotics, computer science, controls, or a closely related field, with a research focus in motion planning, autonomous navigation, or robot decision-making
5+ years of professional experience beyond the PhD, shipping autonomy software in industry -- not just publishing about it
2+ years leading an engineering team, including setting technical direction, managing individual contributors, and delivering complex systems on a timeline
Deep technical expertise in at least two of: sampling-based or optimization-based motion planning (e.g., MPPI, RRT, trajectory optimization), costmap-based navigation, behavior architecture and state machines, vehicle control systems, or simulation/verification frameworks
Experience shipping autonomy to hardware -- you have put your planning and behaviors stack on a real robot and seen it operate in unstructured environments, not just in simulation
Strong partnership instincts -- you know how to work effectively across team boundaries, particularly at the perception-planning interface where two teams must co-own system performance
Clear communication -- you can explain complex technical tradeoffs to engineers, executives, and customers. You write well and think clearly under pressure
Comfort with ambiguity and operational tempo -- defense programs move fast, requirements shift, and field events don't wait. You thrive in this environment

Nice to Have

Experience with off-road or unstructured terrain navigation (not just highway/urban AV)
Familiarity with ROS2 or similar robotics middleware
Background in machine learning for planning or perception-planning integration (learned cost functions, end-to-end planning, foundation models for robotics)
Experience with geospatial planning, satellite imagery-based route planning, or GIS data for autonomy
Prior work in defense, government contracting, or DoD customer engagement
Experience building simulation and log-replay verification systems for autonomous vehicles

Security Clearance

Must be a U.S. Person, as defined under ITAR, and eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance. Active Secret clearance is preferred but not required at the time of hire.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Energy Storage
jobs.description:

Job Description Summary:

The Director of Engineering, Energy Storage leads, mentors, and develops SOLV Energy’s Energy Storage Engineering team. Oversees the design of energy storage systems for utility-scale renewable energy projects, ensuring compliance with technical standards, safety regulations, and project requirements. Drives innovation, implements value engineering strategies, and maintains quality and reliability across all energy storage deliverables.

This role can be fully remote or hybrid, with regular in-office presence in San Diego, CA. Up to 50% travel is required. Specific location details and expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

Job Description:

This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned

Position Responsibilities and Duties:

Department Management/Leadership

Hire, manage, and mentor a diverse team of engineers, focused on energy storage systems and design.
Foster effective communication and collaboration between the Energy Storage Engineering group and cross-functional teams, including internal and external engineers, business development managers, project managers, pre-construction managers, procurement specialists, schedulers, estimators, and construction teams.
Allocate resources effectively to meet project deadlines and ensure optimal team utilization.
Overall management and responsibility of SOLV Energy Storage Engineering team, including establishing and maintaining department goals, budgets, and performance metrics.
Establish and maintain partnerships with a diverse group of third-party Engineers-of-Record (EORs).
Represent SOLV Engineering and management in customer and client meetings.

Technical Oversight

Oversee development of Energy Storage engineering standards and procurement specifications.
Implement and maintain quality control processes to ensure designs comply with all owner, SOLV, AHJ, and vendor requirements.
Proactively identify and resolve potential design and construction challenges and coordinate with various stakeholders to develop cost-effective solutions.
Lead design efforts for interconnection systems, including coordinating utility approvals, ISO and NERC compliance, and energization plans.

Strategic Initiatives

Drive adoption of new technologies and best practices to optimize system performance, reliability, and cost.
Develop innovative, customer-centric engineering solutions that address client needs, reduce cost, and enhance project value.
Represent SOLV Energy team as a technical subject matter expert (SME) during client interviews/meetings as required.
Stay informed on industry best practices and technological advancements in utility-scale energy storage design.
Stay informed on relevant regulations, codes, and guidelines that may impact future SOLV project designs.
Provide SME guidance/consultation to other departments within SOLV, as needed.
Training and Development
Identify training and development needs and provide opportunities for skills enhancement and professional growth.
Develop and mentor staff for career advancement.

Minimum Skills or Experience Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering (preferred).
10+ years of experience in engineering with a focus on Energy Storage, renewables, or power systems in an EPC or Owner/Engineer environment.
Minimum 5+ years of experience in management
Professional Engineer (PE) license is preferred.
Ability to travel up to 50% of the time will be needed.
Proven track record of successfully designing and delivering utility-scale Energy Storage projects.
Strong technical background in protection and control systems, relay settings, and NERC compliance.
Demonstrated experience managing multidisciplinary teams and working in a fast-paced environment.
Technical subject matter expert of applicable codes and standards (NEC, IEEE, IBC, ASCE, NESC, NFPA, utility standards) is preferred.
Extensive experience with grid operations and regulatory requirements (FERC Order 841, IEEE 1547) is preferred.
Strong understanding of fire protection requirements (UL9540, UL9540A, NFPA855).
Deep knowledge of EPC engineering workflows, including design deliverables, submittals, document control, and coordination with engineering partners 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal
Strong leadership, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
Strong sense of urgency.
Ability to travel extensively throughout the United States, up to 50% of the time.

The Director of Engineering, Energy Storage leads, mentors, and develops SOLV Energy’s Energy Storage Engineering team. Oversees the design of energy storage systems for utility-scale renewable energy projects, ensuring compliance with technical standards, safety regulations, and project requirements. Drives innovation, implements value engineering strategies, and maintains quality and reliability across all energy storage deliverables.

This role can be fully remote or hybrid, with regular in-office presence in San Diego, CA. Up to 50% travel is required. Specific location details and expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

Job Description:

This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned

Hire, manage, and mentor a diverse team of engineers, focused on energy storage systems and design.
Foster effective communication and collaboration between the Energy Storage Engineering group and cross-functional teams, including internal and external engineers, business development managers, project managers, pre-construction managers, procurement specialists, schedulers, estimators, and construction teams.
Allocate resources effectively to meet project deadlines and ensure optimal team utilization.
Overall management and responsibility of SOLV Energy Storage Engineering team, including establishing and maintaining department goals, budgets, and performance metrics.
Establish and maintain partnerships with a diverse group of third-party Engineers-of-Record (EORs).
Represent SOLV Engineering and management in customer and client meetings.

Technical Oversight

Oversee development of Energy Storage engineering standards and procurement specifications.
Implement and maintain quality control processes to ensure designs comply with all owner, SOLV, AHJ, and vendor requirements.
Proactively identify and resolve potential design and construction challenges and coordinate with various stakeholders to develop cost-effective solutions.
Lead design efforts for interconnection systems, including coordinating utility approvals, ISO and NERC compliance, and energization plans.

Strategic Initiatives

Drive adoption of new technologies and best practices to optimize system performance, reliability, and cost.
Develop innovative, customer-centric engineering solutions that address client needs, reduce cost, and enhance project value.
Represent SOLV Energy team as a technical subject matter expert (SME) during client interviews/meetings as required.
Stay informed on industry best practices and technological advancements in utility-scale energy storage design.
Stay informed on relevant regulations, codes, and guidelines that may impact future SOLV project designs.
Provide SME guidance/consultation to other departments within SOLV, as needed.

Identify training and development needs and provide opportunities for skills enhancement and professional growth.
Develop and mentor staff for career advancement.

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering (preferred).
10+ years of experience in engineering with a focus on Energy Storage, renewables, or power systems in an EPC or Owner/Engineer environment.

Professional Engineer (PE) license is preferred.
Ability to travel up to 50% of the time will be needed.
Proven track record of successfully designing and delivering utility-scale Energy Storage projects.
Strong technical background in protection and control systems, relay settings, and NERC compliance.
Demonstrated experience managing multidisciplinary teams and working in a fast-paced environment.
Technical subject matter expert of applicable codes and standards (NEC, IEEE, IBC, ASCE, NESC, NFPA, utility standards) is preferred.
Extensive experience with grid operations and regulatory requirements (FERC Order 841, IEEE 1547) is preferred.
Strong understanding of fire protection requirements (UL9540, UL9540A, NFPA855).
Deep knowledge of EPC engineering workflows, including design deliverables, submittals, document control, and coordination with engineering partners 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal
Strong leadership, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.

JOB DESCRIPTION

The Engineering Director, Product Technical Lead is responsible for product engineering for cloud-based solutions for a Tax service line, including Partnership, Corporate, Indirect, and Strategic Tax Services within BDO. This role focuses on a client-centric engineering mindset to deliver high-quality and scalable solutions as the software engineering delivery leader for product development and innovation within BDO Tax.

Job Duties

Tax Technology Business Strategy

Collaborates with senior tax leadership and Product Management leaders to define and execute development strategy for cloud-based tax products for a specific service line for e.g. Partnership, Corporate and Strategic Tax Services
Oversees the technology strategy including architecture, engineering, product design and development within a DT&I product portfolio, ensuring alignment with company goals and delivery of high-quality solutions
Develops and maintains standards, processes, and procedures to ensure product quality and business value

Product Team Leadership

Designs, builds and leads technology development teams with professionals who can excel in a cross-disciplinary environment, fostering a culture of innovation, excellence, and accountability
Drives the growth and professional development of team members, strategically determining resource and staffing needs
Collaborates with BDO National IT regarding governance, infrastructure and security, and with BDO Global and BDO international member firms in the creation, maintenance and deployment of global solutions

Product Development, Architecture & Engineering

Designs, builds, and leads cross-disciplinary technology agile development teams, fostering a culture of innovation, excellence, and accountability
Collaborates with BDO National IT regarding governance, infrastructure, and security, and with BDO Global and international member firms for global solutions deployment
Oversees the development of product portfolios, ensuring projects are delivered on time, within budget, and meet quality standards and business needs
Serves as the technical architect for products and platform-level solutions, designing scalable, maintainable, and secure architectures for complex systems

Stays abreast of emerging technology trends in AI, Cloud and Data domains and evaluate their applicability to firm goals

Risk Management

Ensures compliance with software development best practices, industry standards, and IT standards

jobs.title: Engineering Director
jobs.description:
WRA is seeking an Engineering Director to lead the Engineering Group within our interdisciplinary Riverscapes and Shorelines Team. The desired candidate will collaborate and engage both internally and externally to lead, support, and deliver a diverse range of design projects focused primarily on ecological restoration, with the capability to support a variety of environmental projects across our firm.

You will join our team of restoration design professionals and scientists, including engineers, landscape architects, fluvial geomorphologists, hydrologists, and ecologists. Our projects span a variety of ecosystems across California including San Francisco Bay tidal marshes and living shorelines, Sierra Nevada meadow restoration, Northern California Coast floodplain and salmonid restoration, California Central Coast estuary restoration, and Bay Area and Southern California urban stream rehabilitation. Additionally, our team is actively growing and pursuing restoration work in Oregon. We are passionate about restoring riverine and coastal systems that support healthy and resilient natural and human communities and are invested in the entire restoration process from initial site selection, design and construction to performance monitoring and adaptive management. We also collaborate with our community resilience team to address challenges such as sea-level rise, wildfire resiliency planning, and post-fire recovery.

WRA has a diverse portfolio of projects and clients, including decades-long private entities, public agencies, and non-profit organizations. In addition to our technical expertise, we help clients meet their goals and visions by providing grant fund cultivation, preparing financial models, partnering with investors, and engaging stakeholders.

We envision you working in-person at one of our San Francisco Bay Area offices or in a hybrid arrangement or remote location in this region of California. Other locations may be considered on a case-by-case basis. Regardless of your work arrangement, in-person, remote, or hybrid, you will be excited to collaborate with staff in many technical disciplines across the company.

At WRA, you will have 4 major areas of impact:

Technical Skills:
Provide technical expertise and strategic input to the development and implementation of complex restoration projects
Oversee the production of conceptual plans, construction plan sets, technical specifications, and cost estimates for use in all design phases
Provide construction support and observation services
Leadership:
Utilize experience to provide technical oversight of restoration conceptual plans, construction drawings, specifications, cost estimates, and relevant hydrologic and hydraulics analyses
Supervise, manage, direct and provide oversight of tasks and responsibilities for engineering staff and/or other technical support staff. Mentor and train engineering staff as needed
Oversee project managers and design staff to ensure work quality and that projects meet budgets and deadlines
Foster collaboration within an interdisciplinary team
Assist with strategic planning for the Riverscapes and Shorelines Team
Management:
Develop project work plans and scopes of work
Provide project oversight and schedule monitoring
Manage project budgets and invoicing
Collaborate with our VP of Finance, CEO, and Director of Project Delivery to ensure staff resources are deployed in a productive and profitable manner and assess performance metrics across a diverse project portfolio
Business Development:
Develop regional recognition through networking and events, such as attending and presenting at conferences
Advise clients on project issues to build business
Collaborate with other senior staff to lead proposal efforts with existing and new clients
Participate in various business development events and presenting at conferences
Partner across WRA teams and market segments to assist on multi-disciplinary project pursuits

To be successful in this role, you will need:

To be currently licensed as a Professional Civil Engineer in the state of California
Minimum of 15 years of applicable professional experience
A Bachelor’s degree in civil or environmental engineering, or related field with an emphasis on water resources from an accredited university. A graduate degree in engineering or physical sciences is preferred
Strong written and verbal communication abilities
A passion for ecological restoration
Familiarity with California ecosystems and regulatory environment
Experience developing and managing a portfolio of work
A valid driver’s license and reliable transportation (while WRA has fleet vehicles that can be reserved for field use, during busy field seasons a truck may not be available)

Additional desired qualifications include:

Experience with FEMA Floodplain Development (CLOMR/LOMR) permitting; Certified Floodplain Manager (CFM) certification a plus
Advanced training in river mechanics and restoration
General understanding of geomorphology, including coastal and riverine sediment dynamics

WRA has an established internal leveling system for our staff that maps salary bands that have been informed by market data. Our leveling system is dependent on years of relevant industry experience, education, and the level of responsibility and autonomy at which you’re expected to operate.

The salary range for this position is $167,000-$193,500.

Who are we?

WRA’s an employee-owned environmental consultancy. We are a tenacious team of planners, engineers, and scientists, and we aim to leave the lands we love better than we found them.

Our clients and partners hire us because we’re skilled at navigating through challenging projects involving wildlands, parks, community spaces, and infrastructure. We bring over four decades of expertise, long-standing relationships, and connections to our local communities to make sure that projects are pursued in responsible ways where both people and the environment thrive.

As an organization, we believe that independence and interdependence are not mutually exclusive. We invest in systems, processes, and employee programs to support our staff’s collective engagement and success. At the same time, we encourage our employees to operate with an ownership mindset, taking responsibility for outcomes and being true to our commitments.

WRA’s company vision is to cultivate a sustainable future where people and the environment thrive, and that effort starts first with our staff. We are committed to building a diverse, equitable, and inclusive work environment, and we have developed flexible policies, internal practices, and are investing in programs that prioritize learning and sustainability. We aim to create conditions that allow employees to prioritize their families, lead healthy and balanced lives, and to bring their authentic selves to work every day. We believe that by creating an exceptional workplace, our employees will be able to do their best work and be able to meaningfully contribute to the sustainability of the environment and the communities in which we live.

WRA is an equal opportunity employer, and we are committed to creating a diverse environment. We recruit, employ, train, compensate and promote regardless of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, disability, age, veteran status, and other protected status as required by applicable law.

These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. jobs.description:
Note: By applying to this position you will have an opportunity to share your preferred working location from the following: Sunnyvale, CA, USA; New York, NY, USA; Zürich, Switzerland
. Minimum qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience
15 years of experience in software engineering, with 8 years of experience in a technical engineering role
Experience with protecting systems
Experience in vulnerability management, posture management, or risk analysis

Preferred qualifications:

Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science
Experience motivating others to act by creating a shared sense of outlook or purpose, creating a compelling roadmap for the future, communicating clearly, and employing a collaborative leadership approach
Experience leading complex cross-functional engineering projects
Experience with Agentic AI/ML systems and their unique security implications, including policy-based authorization
Experience providing clarity and alignment across the organization on goals, outcomes, and timelines as well as encouraging engineering excellence and coaching
Entrepreneurial and strategic mindset, growing at the intersection of technology and business with broad technical experience

About The Job

As the Director of Engineering for Product Security (Safe Coding, Cryptography, and Software Supply Chain) in Privacy, Safety, and Security (PSS), you will lead a 100-person global organization across the US, Zurich, and Singapore. You will define the strategic outlook and own the infrastructure responsible for building Google’s secure-by-design development platforms and code integrity systems, ensuring our core software remains resilient at scale.

In this role, you will drive defensive security into the AI era by transitioning Google from reactive vulnerability remediation to automated, secure-by-construction systems. This involves establishing "well-lit paths"—including memory-safe languages like Rust and compiler-enforced defaults—and cryptographic policy engines. To succeed, you will navigate the complex trade-offs between strict security guardrails and developer velocity, executing a multi-year roadmap that protects users as the global developer ecosystem grows in complexity.

To be effective, you will utilize experience as an engineering executive who flexes easily between deep technical execution and high-level strategic alignment. You will be comfortable with ambiguity, possess a strong bias for action, and collaborate exceptionally well across global boundaries. Above all, you will be an advocate for developer productivity and user safety.

The Core team builds the technical foundation behind Google’s flagship products. We are owners and advocates for the underlying design elements, developer platforms, product components, and infrastructure at Google. These are the essential building blocks for excellent, safe, and coherent experiences for our users and drive the pace of innovation for every developer. We look across Google’s products to build central solutions, break down technical barriers and strengthen existing systems. As the Core team, we have a mandate and a unique opportunity to impact important technical decisions across the company.

Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

US: $307000 - $427000 (USD) + 30% bonus target + equity + benefits

Responsibilities

Learn more about benefits at Google .

Lead the strategic outlook and multi-year roadmap for Google's transition to secure-by-construction defenses, ensuring our codebase and supply chain posture scale resiliently alongside AI-driven threats.
Mentor a tiered, multi-site organization of 100 engineers, fostering a culture focused on engineering excellence and psychological safety.
Drive the adoption of 'well-lit paths' across tech stacks, focusing on safe coding, cryptographic hygiene, and software supply chain security.
Partner with Product Area CISOs and engineering executives across Alphabet to align on security roadmaps and drive the upstream adoption of safe-by-default developer platforms.
Define Google's code integrity and software supply chain security strategy while leading company-wide initiatives, including Cryptographic Hygiene OKRs and legacy migrations.

jobs.title: Director of Engineering, Energy Storage
jobs.description:
SOLV Energy is a leading provider of infrastructure services to the power industry, designing, building and maintaining utility scale solar, battery storage and high voltage substation projects nationwide.

Job Description Summary:

The Director of Engineering, Energy Storage leads, mentors, and develops SOLV Energy’s Energy Storage Engineering team. Oversees the design of energy storage systems for utility-scale renewable energy projects, ensuring compliance with technical standards, safety regulations, and project requirements. Drives innovation, implements value engineering strategies, and maintains quality and reliability across all energy storage deliverables.

This role can be fully remote or hybrid, with regular in-office presence in San Diego, CA. Up to 50% travel is required. Specific location details and expectations will be discussed during the interview process.

Job Description:

This job description reflects management's assignment of essential functions; it does not prescribe or restrict the tasks that may be assigned

Position Responsibilities and Duties:

Department Management/Leadership

Hire, manage, and mentor a diverse team of engineers, focused on energy storage systems and design.
Foster effective communication and collaboration between the Energy Storage Engineering group and cross-functional teams, including internal and external engineers, business development managers, project managers, pre-construction managers, procurement specialists, schedulers, estimators, and construction teams.
Allocate resources effectively to meet project deadlines and ensure optimal team utilization.
Overall management and responsibility of SOLV Energy Storage Engineering team, including establishing and maintaining department goals, budgets, and performance metrics.
Establish and maintain partnerships with a diverse group of third-party Engineers-of-Record (EORs).
Represent SOLV Engineering and management in customer and client meetings.

Technical Oversight

Oversee development of Energy Storage engineering standards and procurement specifications.
Implement and maintain quality control processes to ensure designs comply with all owner, SOLV, AHJ, and vendor requirements.
Proactively identify and resolve potential design and construction challenges and coordinate with various stakeholders to develop cost-effective solutions.
Lead design efforts for interconnection systems, including coordinating utility approvals, ISO and NERC compliance, and energization plans.

Strategic Initiatives

Drive adoption of new technologies and best practices to optimize system performance, reliability, and cost.
Develop innovative, customer-centric engineering solutions that address client needs, reduce cost, and enhance project value.
Represent SOLV Energy team as a technical subject matter expert (SME) during client interviews/meetings as required.
Stay informed on industry best practices and technological advancements in utility-scale energy storage design.
Stay informed on relevant regulations, codes, and guidelines that may impact future SOLV project designs.
Provide SME guidance/consultation to other departments within SOLV, as needed.
Training and Development
Identify training and development needs and provide opportunities for skills enhancement and professional growth.
Develop and mentor staff for career advancement.

Minimum Skills or Experience Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering (preferred).
10+ years of experience in engineering with a focus on Energy Storage, renewables, or power systems in an EPC or Owner/Engineer environment.
Minimum 5+ years of experience in management
Professional Engineer (PE) license is preferred.
Ability to travel up to 50% of the time will be needed.
Proven track record of successfully designing and delivering utility-scale Energy Storage projects.
Strong technical background in protection and control systems, relay settings, and NERC compliance.
Demonstrated experience managing multidisciplinary teams and working in a fast-paced environment.
Technical subject matter expert of applicable codes and standards (NEC, IEEE, IBC, ASCE, NESC, NFPA, utility standards) is preferred.
Extensive experience with grid operations and regulatory requirements (FERC Order 841, IEEE 1547) is preferred.
Strong understanding of fire protection requirements (UL9540, UL9540A, NFPA855).
Deep knowledge of EPC engineering workflows, including design deliverables, submittals, document control, and coordination with engineering partners 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, both written and verbal
Strong leadership, organizational, and problem-solving abilities.
Strong sense of urgency.
Ability to travel extensively throughout the United States, up to 50% of the time.

Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. without requiring employer sponsorship now or in the future.

jobs.title: Senior Engineering Manager (Network Value + Outcomes)
jobs.description:
1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access.
We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that.

But we're going further. Over 75,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 1 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens.

We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

Senior Engineering Manager, Payer & Outcomes

Headway's mission is a big one – to build a new mental health care system everyone can access. We've built technology that helps people find great therapists with the first software-enabled national network of providers accepting insurance.

1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but the majority of providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway is building a new mental healthcare system that everyone can access by making it easy for therapists to accept insurance and scale their practice.

Headway was founded in 2019. Since then, we've grown into a diverse, national network of over 60,000 mental healthcare providers across all 50 states who run their practice on our software and have served over 1 million patients. We're a Series D company with over $325m in funding from a16z (Andreessen Horowitz), Accel, GV (formerly Google Ventures), Spark Capital, Thrive Capital, Forerunner Ventures and Health Care Service Corporation.

We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better.

About Engineering At Headway

Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!).

Principles That Guide Us

Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they're facing.
Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iterating.
Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind.
Optimize for trust: We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes.

Tools We Use

Languages: Python 3, TypeScript
Libraries & Frameworks: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, React, Remix, Next.js
Datastores: Postgres, Redis
Infrastructure: AWS (Fargate, ECS, S3, SageMaker and more), Spark and Kafka
Monitoring: Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry
Version Control: Github
Vulnerability Management: Snyk, Semgrep
Cloud Security: Lacework

About This Role

Headway's mission is to build a new mental healthcare system that everyone can access, one that works for patients, providers, and payers alike. Our Payer & Outcomes group is where we prove that model works. We build the systems that answer two questions insurers have never been able to answer well: did the care actually work, and was it worth it?

As Senior Engineering Manager for Payer & Outcomes, you'll lead the two teams that answer them. Outcomes builds our measurement backbone: collecting patient-reported outcomes at scale, tracking symptom improvement and retention to care, and turning that into evidence we can stand behind. Network Value builds the intelligence behind utilization and cost of care, covering patient acuity and segmentation, provider efficiency ranking, and the sub-network logic that routes a patient to the right level of care.

These two teams share data foundations, a measurement stack, and an audience, which is why they sit together under one leader. You'll own delivery on a company-level goal we have publicly committed to: significantly increasing the share of new patients with a baseline outcome measure, without increasing provider churn. That means holding quality and adoption in tension rather than trading one for the other.

You'll grow and mentor a team of roughly eight engineers plus an engineering manager, set the technical and operational roadmap across both pods, and partner daily with Product, Clinical, Data Science, and our payer-facing commercial teams. This is a deeply cross-functional role: your work is what lets Headway move payers from administrative oversight to genuine care partnership.

The stakes here are concrete. Elsewhere in the group we now review clinical notes and prompt providers to put a safety plan in place when a patient shows signs of suicidal risk. At full adoption across our network, that single intervention is estimated to prevent more than 1,000 deaths a year. Your teams build the measurement and targeting layer that decides where interventions like that get aimed, and whether we can prove they worked.

Who You Are

We're looking for an experienced engineering leader who is product-minded, data-informed, and energized by growth. You'll work closely with Engineering Leadership, Product, and Data to shape the future of Headway's payer strategy. There is an unusually direct line from your team's work to whether this model of care survives contact with the market.

In this role you will

Lead, manage, and grow two engineering teams
Own delivery on a company-level outcomes key result, including its guardrails
Set the technical and operational roadmap across measurement, segmentation, and utilization
Develop your team through weekly 1:1s, mentorship, and direct feedback, and develop the manager reporting to you
Partner closely with Product, Clinical, Data Science, and Commercial to iterate quickly and rigorously
Contribute to the broader group and company strategy, not just your own roadmap

Experience We're Seeking

6+ years of engineering management experience at a high-growth startup or scale-up, including managing managers or tech leads
3–5+ years of experience as a software engineer, enough to hold technical direction credibly
A track record of building and leading high-performing teams that delivered business outcomes through technical investment
A strong product mindset and cross-functional relationships that build trust with users and stakeholders
Experience owning an externally-committed metric, with the scope discipline that requires
Comfort with data- and ML-heavy systems: measurement, experimentation, and metric guardrails
Nice to have: healthcare, insurance, or another regulated, high-trust domain
Nice to have: value-based care, quality measurement, or utilization management
Nice to have: prior experience with Python, React, and AWS infrastructure

You'll love this role if you want to

Lead the teams that decide whether a new model of mental healthcare can be proven, not just described
Own a number the company reports externally, with the autonomy that comes with it
Build an engineering management layer beneath you rather than inherit a finished org

Our interview process

After you apply to Headway, here are some details of what to expect during the interview process.

Initial screen: You'll connect with someone in recruiting so you can learn more about the team, Headway's mission and exciting growth, and we can get a better idea of your background.
First rounds: You'll meet with an engineering leader on the team to go deeper into your team and people leadership experience. You'll also complete an AI Coding round — a collaborative session where we're less focused on syntax and more on how you think through problems and work with AI tools in a technical context.
Final rounds: You'll meet team members across product and engineering leadership for multiple behavioral interviews and one more technical interview (System Design), leaving you with a fuller picture of what it's like to work at Headway.
References and the Offer: Our favorite part of the process! We'll send over all of the details, including specifics on employee equity, and congratulatory messages from excited future team members!

Compensation And Benefits

The expected base pay range for this position is $265,200 - 331,500, based on a variety of factors including qualifications, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for performance-based variable compensation and an equity grant, depending on the position and level.

We are committed to offering a comprehensive and competitive total rewards package, including robust health and wellness benefits, retirement savings, and meaningful ownership opportunities through equity. Compensation decisions are made holistically, ensuring fairness and alignment with market benchmarks while recognizing individual contributions and potential.

Buildout is the AI deal engine for CRE brokerages, automating every step from first contact to commission. While brokers focus on relationships and winning listings, Buildout handles the workflows behind the scenes, turning manual processes into intelligent, scalable systems. Trusted by over 50,000 brokers, Buildout powers more profitable deals from lead to close. Learn more at www.buildout.com.

The Opportunity

Buildout is hiring a Director of Engineering to lead the performance and execution of our engineering organization. You’ll manage a team of engineers and technical leads, creating the clarity, accountability, and support they need to do their best work. You will own the people and operating systems behind a healthy engineering organization, from coaching and performance management to staffing, planning, delivery, and cross-functional partnership. You’ll help the team thoughtfully adopt AI-assisted development practices that improve developer productivity, software quality, and delivery speed.

This role is an important partner to our SVP of Engineering. While the SVP of Engineering remains focused on technology strategy, architecture, and long-term direction, you will turn that direction into an effective, predictable, and high-performing engineering operation.

What You'll Own

Engineering Leadership & Talent

Lead the day-to-day performance and development of our engineering organization, making sure every engineer knows what good looks like, where they stand, and how they can grow.
Manage and coach engineers and technical leads, giving them the context and support to make good decisions without needing you in the middle of every one.
Recognize and grow strong performers, develop future technical leaders, and address performance concerns directly and early.
Own engineering hiring and onboarding, building the talent and team structure we need to meet the needs of the business.

Delivery & Operational Excellence

Create clear accountability for engineering delivery across teams, with enough structure to make execution predictable without slowing people down.
Maintain a clear view of capacity, commitments, dependencies, and risk so problems surface early and leadership isn't surprised.
Step into cross-team dependencies, competing priorities, and delivery challenges when teams need help getting unstuck.
Use AI as a force multiplier for the engineering organization, setting clear expectations for adoption and turning what works into repeatable practices across coding, testing, documentation, automation, and the broader development lifecycle.
Drive measurable improvements in developer productivity and team effectiveness while maintaining strong standards for software quality and responsible AI use.

Product & Business Partnership

Serve as Product's primary partner for engineering execution, bringing a clear view of capacity, feasibility, risk, and tradeoffs into roadmap and prioritization decisions.
Help turn product priorities into realistic engineering commitments—and make the tradeoffs clear when everything can't be a priority.
Communicate risks early and honestly, bringing problems forward with enough context to make good decisions.
Be a steady escalation point when delivery, staffing, or organizational issues cross team boundaries or don't have an obvious answer.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 Days:

Learn the Organization

Build trust with engineers, technical leads, Product, and executive stakeholders.
Understand team structures, responsibilities, delivery processes, and technical ownership.
Learn existing strengths, bottlenecks, and organizational pain points.
Observe planning, delivery, and cross-functional interactions before making major changes.

Establish Leadership Presence

Begin regular one-on-ones with all direct reports.
Understand individual career goals, concerns, and performance histories.
Build credibility as a leader who listens, follows through, and removes obstacles.

First 90 Days:

Become The Primary Operational Leader

Become the first point of escalation for delivery and personnel issues.
Establish visibility into delivery risks, team health, and organizational capacity.
Build strong working relationships with Product leadership.
Create consistency in communication and expectations across teams.

Identify Organizational Improvements

Recommend targeted improvements to execution, planning, staffing, or team structure.
Clarify ownership boundaries where necessary.
Ensure technical leads are focused on technical leadership rather than people-management responsibilities.

First 6 Months:

Improve Organizational Execution

Delivery risks are identified and addressed proactively.
Cross-team dependencies are managed effectively.
Product views the Director as the primary engineering execution partner.
Engineers receive consistent coaching, feedback, and career development.

Reduce SVP of Engineering Operational Involvement

Personnel issues are handled without SVP of Engineering intervention.
Delivery escalations are routed through the Director.
Team-level execution concerns are resolved without executive involvement.
The SVP of Engineering is spending significantly less time on organizational and operational concerns.

First Year:

Build a High-Performing Engineering Organization

Engineering delivery is predictable and transparent.
Strong accountability exists across teams without excessive process.
Performance management is consistent and effective.
High performers are identified, developed, and retained.
Underperformance is addressed quickly and professionally.

Enable the SVP of Engineering Role

The SVP of Engineering focuses primarily on technology strategy, architecture, executive leadership, and long-term planning.
The Director serves as the trusted operational leader of the engineering organization.
Engineering and Product leadership operate as effective partners.
The organization scales successfully without increasing executive involvement in day-to-day operations.

What Makes a Great Candidate

You make expectations unmistakable. People rarely leave a conversation with you wondering what matters, who owns what, or what happens next. You create clarity without turning every problem into a new process.
You make teams run better. You look for ways to make the team faster, more effective, and more consistent without adding unnecessary processes. You see AI as a force multiplier and know how to turn it from a tool into a meaningful part of how an engineering team builds, solves problems, and delivers.
You coach before you rescue. Your instinct is not to take over when someone struggles. You ask the right questions, give direct feedback, and help people build the judgment to solve the next problem themselves.
You can hold the line without hardening the room. You are comfortable addressing missed commitments, performance concerns, and difficult tradeoffs. You are direct without being careless and empathetic without avoiding accountability.
You see around corners. You notice when a staffing gap, unclear ownership boundary, or unresolved dependency is likely to become a larger problem. You raise it early and help the right people act before it becomes an emergency.
You translate between Product and Engineering. You can hear an ambitious product goal and identify the engineering choices beneath it. You help both sides understand capacity, risk, and tradeoffs.
You likely also have:
Experience leading and developing engineers across multiple product teams
Experience with performance management, hiring, and career development.
Experience leading technical leads and senior engineers
Enough technical depth to understand engineering tradeoffs and earn the trust of experienced developers, without needing to be the primary architect.
Demonstrated success improving organizational effectiveness while maintaining a strong engineering culture.

Location: This is a fully remote role open across most of the US.
